functions.funcDef: Provide thrust for all phases of flight (§5.1.1).
functions.subDef: Four podded turbofans provide thrust for all phases of flight (§5.1.1). Independence: left/right engine pairs in separate zones, services not commingled outboard of wing root (§5.1.5).

functions.funcDef: Provide thrust for all phases of flight (§5.1.1).
functions.subName: Provide reverse thrust on the ground
functions.subDef: Thrust reversers on the two inboard engines; deployment inhibited in flight by weight-on-wheels and radio-altimeter agreement (§5.1.2).

functions.funcDef: Position primary and secondary surfaces to provide control authority across the flight envelope (§5.3.1).
functions.subDef: Roll by two-segment ailerons and multi-function spoilers (§5.3.2); ailerons on hydraulic B and C, dual actuation (§5.3.2).

functions.funcDef: Position primary and secondary surfaces to provide control authority across the flight envelope (§5.3.1).
functions.subDef: Pitch by all-moving trimmable horizontal stabiliser with elevators; elevators on hydraulic A and C (§5.3.2); mechanical reversion to stabiliser trim (§5.3.2).

functions.funcDef: Position primary and secondary surfaces to provide control authority across the flight envelope (§5.3.1).
functions.subDef: Yaw by split rudder in upper and lower segments, each with its own actuation and hydraulic supply A/B (§5.3.2); mechanical reversion to lower rudder segment (§5.3.2).

functions.funcDef: Position primary and secondary surfaces to provide control authority across the flight envelope (§5.3.1).
functions.subDef: Double-slotted Fowler flaps in four sections and full-span leading-edge slats, driven by two independent power drive units through a common torque shaft with asymmetry brakes (§5.3.2).

functions.funcName: Support and decelerate on the ground
functions.funcDef: Support the aircraft on the ground, absorb landing/taxi loads, and provide braking and directional control on the ground (§5.6.1).
functions.subName: Support aircraft on the ground and absorb landing loads
functions.subDef: One twin-wheel nose unit and six three-wheel main bogies; retraction/extension by hydraulic A with free-fall alternate (§5.6.2). Flotation sized for semi-prepared surface (§5.6.2).

functions.funcName: Support and decelerate on the ground
functions.funcDef: Support the aircraft on the ground, absorb landing/taxi loads, and provide braking and directional control on the ground (§5.6.1).
functions.subDef: Carbon multi-disc braking, normally hydraulic B, alternate A, accumulator-supported emergency braking, anti-skid per wheel pair (§5.6.2).

functions.funcName: Support and decelerate on the ground
functions.funcDef: Support the aircraft on the ground, absorb landing/taxi loads, and provide braking and directional control on the ground (§5.6.1).
functions.subDef: Hydraulic nose wheel steering commanded from tillers and rudder pedals, with mechanical disconnect for towing (§5.6.2).

functions.funcName: Provide payload access and pressure-boundary closure at the nose
functions.funcDef: Provide straight-in nose access to the hold and form part of the pressure boundary when closed (§5.7.1).
functions.subName: Latch and lock the nose door closed
functions.subDef: Twelve rotary latches on a common torque shaft, eight independent locking pins on a separate actuator/supply, with pressure interlock in series with the unlock command (§5.7.2, §5.7.3). Structure load path excluded — treated as structure (§5.7.3).

functions.funcDef: Receive, position and restrain a single blade and maintain restraint through all flight and ground load cases (§5.8.1).
functions.subDef: Two tension straps per saddle across nine saddles, electric-winch tensioned and mechanically locked, with a single instrumented tension monitoring loop (§5.8.2). Hold floor hard points excluded — no redundancy, treated as structure (§5.8.3).

functions.funcDef: Condition and distribute air to flight deck and hold and control pressure differential across the fuselage (§5.9.1).
functions.subDef: Two digital controllers driving two outflow valves, pneumatic backup mode, independent positive/negative mechanical relief (§5.9.2).

functions.funcDef: Condition and distribute air to flight deck and hold and control pressure differential across the fuselage (§5.9.1).
functions.subName: Condition and distribute air to flight deck and hold
functions.subDef: Two air cycle packs supplied from four engine bleeds through a cross-bleed manifold; flight deck and hold as separate conditioning zones (§5.9.2).

functions.funcName: Protect surfaces and probes from ice
functions.funcDef: Prevent or remove ice accretion where accretion would be unacceptable, for flight in the icing envelope (§5.10.1).
functions.subName: Protect wings and inlets from ice by bleed air
functions.subDef: Wing leading edges and engine inlet cowls protected by hot bleed air through piccolo distribution, from either side via cross-bleed manifold (§5.10.2, §5.10.3).

functions.funcName: Protect surfaces and probes from ice
functions.funcDef: Prevent or remove ice accretion where accretion would be unacceptable, for flight in the icing envelope (§5.10.1).
functions.subName: Protect stabilisers, probes and windshields by electrical heating
functions.subDef: Stabiliser leading edges electrically heated in six independently controlled zones; probes, static ports, windshields and two ice detectors electrically heated and individually monitored (§5.10.2).

functions.funcDef: Acquire, process and present the information the crew needs to fly, navigate and manage the aircraft, and host alerting (§5.11.1).
functions.subName: Acquire and present flight, navigation and system information
functions.subDef: Four display units and two head-up displays driven by three display processing units on dual redundant network; three air data inertial reference units; independent standby instrument on DC essential bus (§5.11.2).

functions.funcDef: Acquire, process and present the information the crew needs to fly, navigate and manage the aircraft, and host alerting (§5.11.1).
functions.subDef: Alerting system consolidates every system's status into a single prioritised crew alert list with procedures, driven by two independent processing channels (§5.11.2).

functions.funcDef: Detect fire and overheat where they must be detected, and provide the means to extinguish or suppress them (§5.12.1).
functions.subDef: Dual-loop continuous detection per engine nacelle and APU with AND logic degrading to single-loop; overheat detection on bleed ducts and main gear bays; nine-station hold smoke detection (§5.12.2).

functions.funcDef: Detect fire and overheat where they must be detected, and provide the means to extinguish or suppress them (§5.12.1).
functions.subDef: Two extinguisher bottles per engine pair cross-plumbed to either nacelle; single dedicated APU bottle discharged automatically on the ground unattended (§5.12.2). Hold: detection but no suppression fitted — recorded as an assumption to substantiate (§5.12.2).

functions.funcDef: Supply breathing oxygen to the flight crew for loss of pressurisation, smoke and fume events, and the ensuing descent and diversion (§5.13.1).
functions.subName: Supply breathing oxygen to the flight crew
functions.subDef: Two high-pressure cylinders on a common manifold with crossover, feeding four quick-donning full-face masks with demand regulators; no passenger oxygen — hold not occupied in flight (§5.13.2).

fha.fcDesc: Uncommanded thrust change (one or more engines commanding thrust different from intended)
fha.effAc: Uncommanded thrust, if asymmetric from an outboard engine at the 28 m moment arm, produces a yawing/rolling moment demanding significant rudder authority; if a rapid uncommanded increase or decrease it disturbs the trajectory and, at low speed/low altitude (take-off, approach), reduces the margin available for recovery.
fha.effCrew: Crew detect via engine parameter display and aircraft response; must counter with rudder/thrust-lever action and identify the affected engine. Workload increase, significant if the event is at low altitude or asymmetric outboard.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; flight crew only.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Uncommanded asymmetric thrust from an outboard engine at the 28 m sizing moment arm produces a large yawing moment and a large reduction in safety margins/functional capability with high crew workload, particularly at low speed; effects support Hazardous rather than Catastrophic since directional authority is sized for the asymmetric outboard case. Engineer to confirm per-phase worst case. [anchor HAZ-1 — Hazardous] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Partial loss of thrust generation — asymmetric (loss of thrust from one engine)
fha.effAc: Loss of one engine produces asymmetric thrust; an outboard failure at the 28 m moment arm is the directional-control sizing case and is countered by the sized rudder authority. Aircraft is designed to continue to a suitable aerodrome after loss of any one engine at or after V1. Reduced performance and reduced climb/obstacle margins.
fha.effCrew: Crew identify the failed engine, apply rudder to hold heading, and complete engine-out procedure; increased workload but within the designed engine-out case.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; flight crew only.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Single-engine loss is the designed dispatch case with directional authority sized for the outboard failure and continuation to a suitable aerodrome; effects are a significant reduction in safety margins and significant increase in crew workload — Major. Engineer to confirm the take-off/V1 phase is not more severe once performance data are available. [anchor MAJ-1 — Major] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of thrust generation (loss of thrust from all four engines)
fha.effAc: Loss of all propulsive thrust; the aircraft cannot sustain flight and cannot reach a suitable aerodrome except by glide, with loss of the airplane the expected outcome outside of a fortuitous forced-landing.
fha.effCrew: Crew face maximum workload attempting relight/forced landing with no thrust available.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; flight crew only.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Total loss of thrust from all four engines results in inability to sustain flight and loss of the airplane — Catastrophic. Engineer to confirm. [anchor CAT-1 — Catastrophic] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Inadvertent reverse thrust deployment (uncommanded deployment of an inboard reverser)
fha.effAc: Reversers are fitted to the two inboard engines only; in-flight deployment is inhibited by weight-on-wheels and radio-altimeter agreement with a mechanical sleeve lock. An in-flight inadvertent deployment (if the inhibits are defeated) produces a sudden thrust/drag asymmetry and disturbance from an inboard station (approx. 0.18 semi-span); on the ground it disturbs directional control during the landing roll.
fha.effCrew: Crew must recognise and counter the asymmetry and manage the affected engine; workload significant, more severe if in flight at low speed.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; flight crew only.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Severity depends on whether the in-flight inhibit (WoW + radio-altimeter agreement + mechanical sleeve lock) is credited as defeated for this condition, and on the flight-phase worst case; the SDD states the inhibits but the FHA cannot assume their integrity. Effect magnitude (in-flight inboard-reverser deployment vs. ground-only) needed before a class is committed — left empty pending that engineering judgement.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Partial loss of reverse thrust — asymmetric (loss of reverse thrust from one inboard reverser on the ground)
fha.effAc: Reverse thrust available from the two inboard engines only; loss of one produces asymmetric reverse thrust during the ground roll and reduces total decelerating thrust, eroding the margin between the 1,800 m landing distance requirement and the ~1,080 m predicted rollout on a semi-prepared surface. Braking (dual hydraulic plus accumulator, anti-skid) remains the primary decelerating means.
fha.effCrew: Crew counter the asymmetry with rudder/steering and rely on wheel braking; increased workload during the roll.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; flight crew only.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Reverse thrust is a supplementary decelerating means with wheel braking sized to the landing case and a stated margin to the requirement; loss of one inboard reverser gives asymmetric reverse and a slight reduction in the deceleration margin with a slight workload increase — proposed Minor. Engineer to confirm against the braking-degradation assessment and the semi-prepared-surface margin. [anchor MIN-1 — Minor] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of reverse thrust
fha.effAc: No reverse-thrust deceleration available on landing rollout; ground deceleration reverts entirely to wheel braking. With the 1,800 m landing-distance requirement against a predicted ~1,080 m rollout, and brake accumulator sized to six full applications, the margin is reduced but a deceleration means remains available.
fha.effCrew: Crew apply maximum wheel braking; increased workload and reduced stopping margin on the semi-prepared strip.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants affected.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Reverse thrust is a supplementary deceleration means; wheel braking remains available with sized margin, giving a significant reduction in deceleration margin rather than loss of the function. [anchor MAJ-1 — Major] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Erroneous roll response to command
fha.effAc: Aircraft rolls in a manner different from the crew's command, potentially opposite in sense or magnitude; departure from the intended flight path with potential for loss of control if not arrested.
fha.effCrew: Crew must recognise the erroneous response and counter it; high workload under a startle condition, with reversion to degraded control laws as annunciated.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants affected.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: An erroneous roll response is a lateral upset that, if not arrested, can lead to loss of aircraft control. [anchor CAT-1 — Catastrophic] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Uncommanded roll motion
fha.effAc: Aircraft rolls without a crew command; uncommanded departure in the lateral axis with potential for loss of control if not arrested.
fha.effCrew: Crew must detect the uncommanded motion and counter it manually; high workload under a startle condition.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants affected.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: An uncommanded roll is a lateral upset that, if not arrested, can lead to loss of aircraft control. [anchor CAT-1 — Catastrophic] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Undetected roll response error
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants affected.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Crew-unaware variant: the SDD does not state the detection means for a roll response error nor the aircraft effect that results once the crew take no corrective action; without the resulting effect the class cannot be derived. Needs the crew-detection/alerting basis and the undetected-case aircraft effect.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Undetected uncommanded roll motion
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants affected.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Crew-unaware variant: the SDD does not state how an uncommanded roll would go undetected nor the aircraft effect once the crew take no corrective action; without the resulting effect the class cannot be derived. Needs the crew-detection/alerting basis and the undetected-case aircraft effect.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Partial loss of roll control authority
fha.effAc: Reduced roll authority; aircraft still controllable in roll but with reduced manoeuvre margin and degraded response to lateral upset, most demanding in the engine-out and blade-loaded directional-control case.
fha.effCrew: Increased workload to maintain wings-level and track; degraded law annunciated.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupant effect.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Reduced roll authority is a significant reduction in functional capability with a significant increase in crew workload, but roll control is retained; effects do not reach a large reduction in safety margins. [anchor MAJ-1 — Major] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of roll control
fha.effAc: No means of roll control by any surface; aircraft cannot be manoeuvred or trimmed in roll and departs controlled flight.
fha.effCrew: Crew unable to control aircraft in the roll axis.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupant effect.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Complete loss of a primary flight-control axis prevents continued controlled flight and results in loss of the aeroplane. [anchor CAT-1 — Catastrophic] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Erroneous pitch response to command
fha.effAc: Pitch surface responds differently from the commanded input, producing a pitch attitude/flight-path excursion; potential to reach structural or envelope limits before the crew recovers.
fha.effCrew: Crew must detect the erroneous response and counter it; degraded law annunciated; workload increased during recovery.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupant effect.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: An erroneous pitch response is a large reduction in safety margins in the pitch axis with excessive crew workload to counter it, but the crew is aware and can act to recover. [anchor HAZ-1 — Hazardous] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Uncommanded pitch motion
fha.effAc: Pitch surface moves without a crew or autopilot command, producing an uncommanded pitch/flight-path excursion; potential to reach structural or envelope limits before recovery.
fha.effCrew: Crew must recognise the uncommanded motion and arrest it; workload increased during recovery.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupant effect.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: An uncommanded pitch excursion is a large reduction in safety margins in the pitch axis with excessive crew workload to arrest and recover, with the crew aware and able to act. [anchor HAZ-1 — Hazardous] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Undetected pitch response error
fha.effAc: Pitch responds differently from intended with no crew awareness; the crew continue normally and take no corrective action, so the excursion develops toward loss of control before it is recognised.
fha.effCrew: Crew continue their duties normally and take no action; no awareness cue assumed.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupant effect.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: With the error undetected the crew take no corrective action and the pitch excursion develops unchecked toward loss of controlled flight and loss of the aeroplane. [anchor CAT-1 — Catastrophic] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Undetected uncommanded pitch motion
fha.phases: Takeoff, Climb, Cruise, Descent, Approach, Landing
fha.effAc: Uncommanded pitch excursion develops without crew awareness; departure from intended flight path and possible exceedance of structural or aerodynamic limits before the crew can intervene.
fha.effCrew: No cue that a pitch input is being applied; crew do not act until aircraft response is manifest, by which point recovery margin may be lost.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; flight crew only.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: — [anchor CAT-1 — Catastrophic] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Partial loss of pitch control authority
fha.phases: Takeoff, Climb, Cruise, Descent, Approach, Landing
fha.effAc: Reduced pitch authority; ability to hold or change flight path degraded, with reduced safety margins particularly at forward centre-of-gravity with a full-length blade payload.
fha.effCrew: Increased workload to fly and configure the aircraft with degraded pitch response; degraded control law annunciated.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; flight crew only.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: — [anchor HAZ-1 — Hazardous] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of pitch control
fha.phases: Takeoff, Climb, Cruise, Descent, Approach, Landing
fha.effAc: No means to control the pitch axis; aircraft cannot be maintained on a controllable flight path and loss of the aircraft results.
fha.effCrew: No effective pitch control available through any path; crew unable to arrest departure from controlled flight.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; flight crew only.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: — [anchor CAT-1 — Catastrophic] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Erroneous yaw response to command
fha.phases: Takeoff, Climb, Cruise, Descent, Approach, Landing
fha.effAc: Yaw surface responds differently from commanded, producing sideslip and lateral-directional excursion; safety margins reduced, aggravated in the outboard-engine-out directional-control case at the 28 m moment arm.
fha.effCrew: Increased workload to detect and counter the erroneous yaw response and stabilise the flight path.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; flight crew only.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: — [anchor HAZ-1 — Hazardous] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Uncommanded yaw motion
fha.phases: Takeoff, Climb, Cruise, Descent, Approach, Landing
fha.effAc: Uncommanded yaw/sideslip develops without a crew command; large reduction in safety margins and potential departure from controlled flight if not promptly countered, worst at high dynamic pressure.
fha.effCrew: Crew must recognise and counter an uncommanded yaw input; high workload and reduced time to react.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; flight crew only.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: — [anchor CAT-1 — Catastrophic] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Undetected yaw response error (crew unaware) — erroneous yaw response to command with no crew awareness or correction
fha.effAc: Aircraft develops a yaw/sideslip excursion that does not match the commanded response; with the crew unaware and taking no corrective action the excursion is not arrested, degrading directional control and, at low speed/high asymmetry, threatening controllability.
fha.effCrew: Crew continue duties normally and take no action regarding the error; misleading directional behaviour not identified in time.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no passengers carried.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Uncorrected erroneous yaw with no crew awareness can develop into an unrecoverable excursion / loss of the airplane. [anchor CAT-1 — Catastrophic] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Undetected uncommanded yaw motion (crew unaware) — uncommanded yaw/rudder motion with no crew awareness or correction
fha.effAc: Uncommanded yaw input drives a sideslip/heading excursion; with the crew unaware and taking no corrective action the excursion is not arrested, degrading directional control and threatening controllability at critical phases.
fha.effCrew: Crew continue duties normally and take no action; uncommanded directional motion not identified in time.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no passengers carried.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Uncorrected uncommanded yaw with no crew awareness can develop into an unrecoverable excursion / loss of the airplane. [anchor CAT-1 — Catastrophic] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Partial loss of yaw control authority — reduced directional control authority (e.g. single rudder segment supply lost)
fha.effAc: Reduced yaw authority; per the sizing case a single rudder-segment supply loss must still leave sufficient authority to counter the outboard-engine-out asymmetry, so a single loss is a reduction in safety margin rather than loss of control; larger reductions increase difficulty in the engine-out and blade-loaded case.
fha.effCrew: Crew aware via degraded-control annunciation and control feel; increased workload maintaining directional control, particularly in the asymmetric-thrust case.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no passengers carried.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Large reduction in directional-control safety margin in the sizing engine-out / blade-loaded case, with increased crew workload. [anchor HAZ-1 — Hazardous] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of yaw control — directional control unavailable by any means
fha.effAc: No directional control; the sizing outboard-engine-out asymmetry at the 28 m moment arm cannot be countered and heading/sideslip cannot be controlled, leading to loss of the airplane.
fha.effCrew: Crew aware but unable to arrest the excursion; no means of directional control available.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no passengers carried.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Total loss of directional control leaves the engine-out asymmetry uncountered — loss of the airplane. [anchor CAT-1 — Catastrophic] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Uncommanded high-lift augmentation — flap/slat movement to a position other than commanded
fha.effAc: Uncommanded change in high-lift configuration alters lift, drag and pitch trim and can produce a configuration inappropriate to speed/phase; asymmetry brakes constrain runaway but an uncommanded position change reduces safety margins, notably at high speed (slat/flap overspeed) or on approach.
fha.effCrew: Crew aware via configuration indication and handling change; increased workload managing the unexpected configuration and speed.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no passengers carried.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Uncommanded high-lift configuration change at an inappropriate speed/phase produces a large reduction in safety margins. [anchor HAZ-1 — Hazardous] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Erroneous high-lift augmentation (uncommanded extension/retraction or runaway to a position other than commanded)
fha.effAc: Surface position differs from the commanded/scheduled configuration; uncommanded change of lift and drag alters attained speeds and margins to stall or overspeed for the phase; asymmetry drives a rolling/yawing moment requiring corrective control.
fha.effCrew: Crew detect the discrepancy via configuration/position indication and alerting, revert to a known configuration and manage speed; increased workload during a critical phase.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants other than flight crew.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Uncommanded high-lift change during take-off or approach produces a large reduction in safety margin (proximity to stall/overspeed and asymmetric moment) at a critical phase. [anchor HAZ-1 — Hazardous] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Partial loss of high-lift augmentation — asymmetric (one section fails to track, asymmetry brake engages)
fha.effAc: Asymmetric lift produces a rolling moment and increased drag on the affected side; attained take-off/landing speeds increase and control margin is reduced; asymmetry brakes arrest further travel leaving surfaces mismatched.
fha.effCrew: Asymmetry/position discretes annunciate; crew apply lateral control, select an appropriate configuration and revised speeds, and manage a longer field requirement.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants other than flight crew.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Asymmetric high-lift loss at take-off or landing gives a large reduction in safety margin from the rolling moment combined with degraded low-speed performance at a critical phase. [anchor HAZ-1 — Hazardous] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Partial loss of high-lift augmentation — symmetric (reduced high-lift travel on both sides)
fha.effAc: Both sides deliver reduced high-lift; attained take-off and landing speeds increase and field-length requirement grows symmetrically without an asymmetric moment.
fha.effCrew: Position indication annunciates reduced configuration; crew revise speeds and field performance and manage the degraded schedule.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants other than flight crew.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot classify without the retained high-lift capability threshold and the resulting take-off/landing speed and field-length margin against the 1,800 m semi-prepared requirement (predicted rollout ~1,080 m); the degree of partial loss determines whether the margin reduction is significant (Major) or large (Hazardous).. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Undetected partial loss of high-lift augmentation — asymmetric (crew unaware; no annunciation of the mismatch)
fha.effAc: Asymmetric high-lift with no crew awareness; the aircraft is flown at planned configuration speeds that no longer match the degraded low-speed capability, with an uncorrected rolling moment reducing margin to loss of control near the ground.
fha.effCrew: Crew continue normal duties and take no corrective action regarding the undetected asymmetry; planned speeds and configuration are unrevised.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants other than flight crew.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Undetected asymmetric high-lift loss at take-off or landing, flown at unrevised speeds with an uncorrected rolling moment near the ground, can lead to loss of control with no crew mitigation. [anchor CAT-1 — Catastrophic] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of high-lift augmentation (flaps and slats fail to extend / remain stowed)
fha.effAc: Take-off and landing must be flown in a clean/degraded configuration at substantially higher speeds; take-off and landing field-length requirements increase materially against the 1,800 m semi-prepared limit; approach and touchdown speeds and energy rise.
fha.effCrew: Configuration/position indication and alerting annunciate the failure; crew apply the flapless/degraded-configuration procedure with revised speeds and field performance; significant workload increase.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants other than flight crew.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Total loss of high-lift forces a high-speed clean-configuration landing that materially erodes the field-length margin against the 1,800 m semi-prepared requirement — a large reduction in functional capability and safety margin. [anchor HAZ-1 — Hazardous] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Partial loss of ground support and landing-load absorption
fha.effAc: One or more of the six main bogies / twenty tyres degraded; reduced flotation and load-spreading on the semi-prepared surface, uneven load path into the airframe, possible runway excursion or structural overload at touchdown. Crew aware via gear position / brake-temp / tyre-pressure indication and assumed to continue or reject as appropriate.
fha.effCrew: Increased workload managing a degraded gear on an unprepared surface; directional-control corrections during rollout.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants affected in flight.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Effects as stated — degraded flotation/load-spreading on a semi-prepared strip with crew aware — support a significant reduction in functional capability and a significant increase in crew workload, but not a large reduction in safety margins for a partial, annunciated degradation. [anchor MAJ-1 — Major] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Undetected partial loss of ground support and landing-load absorption
fha.effAc: Degraded bogie/tyre or flotation capability with the crew unaware; crew continue normal duties and take no action. On the semi-prepared surface the reduced load-spreading is not compensated, raising the likelihood of gear collapse, runway excursion or structural overload during the landing/take-off ground roll.
fha.effCrew: No action taken because the degradation is not annunciated; crew continue normally.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants affected in flight.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot classify from the function definition alone: the aircraft-level outcome of an UNDETECTED partial gear degradation depends on how much support/flotation margin remains and whether the semi-prepared-surface landing can still be completed without gear collapse or overload — margins not stated in the provided functions. Need the residual load-path / flotation margin and the failure of the dual downlock / condition sensing to establish whether the unaware case is Major or Hazardous.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of ground support and landing-load absorption
fha.effAc: No ground support or landing-load absorption available; the aircraft cannot be supported on its gear at touchdown, leading to fuselage/structural contact with the surface, collapse and loss of the airplane during landing or the take-off ground roll.
fha.effCrew: Crew unable to prevent the outcome; no means to compensate for total loss of ground support at touchdown.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants affected in flight.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Effects as stated — complete inability to support the aircraft on the ground at touchdown, with structural contact and collapse — support loss of the airplane. [anchor CAT-1 — Catastrophic] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Uncommanded ground deceleration — asymmetric
fha.effAc: Asymmetric uncommanded braking/deceleration produces a yawing moment during the ground roll; on the semi-prepared strip with ~720 m margin between the 1,800 m requirement and ~1,080 m predicted rollout, a directional excursion off the prepared area or loss of directional control is credible, with possible gear/tyre overload.
fha.effCrew: Crew must detect and counter an uncommanded yaw with steering/differential-brake and rudder inputs during a high-workload ground phase; corrective action assumed but demanding on an unprepared surface.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants affected in flight.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Effects as stated — an uncommanded asymmetric decelerating moment during the ground roll on a narrow semi-prepared strip — support a large reduction in safety margins (directional control / runway excursion) with excessive crew workload to counter. Confirm against the directional-control sizing case and available lateral margin on the strip. [anchor HAZ-1 — Hazardous] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Uncommanded ground directional control
fha.effAc: Uncommanded steering/directional input produces a heading deviation during the ground roll on a semi-prepared strip; at speed this risks departure from the prepared surface.
fha.effCrew: Crew perceives the yaw/heading cue and counters via steering, differential braking and rudder; workload increases sharply at high ground speed.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied; no occupant effect.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — The provided function definition ("Provide ground directional control") and SDD establish that steering deviation is countered by the crew, but the magnitude/authority of an uncommanded input and its recoverability at the sizing ground speeds are not given, so an aircraft-level effect cannot be bounded to select between Major and Hazardous without that data.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Erroneous ground directional control
fha.effAc: Erroneous directional response to a crew steering command yields incorrect heading tracking during the ground roll on a semi-prepared strip, risking lateral departure from the prepared surface.
fha.effCrew: Crew observes the aircraft not tracking as commanded and reverts to differential braking / rudder to hold centreline under elevated workload.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied; no occupant effect.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — No SF-009-M2 condition exists in the current FCIM (only SF-009-M is defined), and the function definition does not quantify the erroneous-response magnitude, so an aircraft-level effect cannot be bounded to select a class; source condition needs confirmation before classifying.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Partial loss of ground directional control
fha.effAc: Reduced ability to hold runway/strip centreline during the ground roll; heading control degraded but still achievable using differential braking and rudder within remaining authority. Risk of lateral excursion on the 1,800 m semi-prepared strip against a ~1,080 m predicted rollout margin.
fha.effCrew: Increased workload to maintain directional control by differential braking and rudder pedal input; crew aware through heading and yaw cues.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants affected.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Significant reduction in ground directional-control capability requiring increased crew workload with differential braking/rudder remaining; effects stated support a significant, not large, reduction in safety margins on a semi-prepared surface. [anchor MAJ-1 — Major] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of ground directional control
fha.effAc: No nose-wheel steering directional control; heading held only by differential braking and rudder while the latter remains effective. Elevated risk of runway/strip lateral excursion, particularly at low speed or on the semi-prepared surface where rudder authority is limited and margin against the 1,800 m requirement is finite.
fha.effCrew: Crew aware through heading deviation and steering cues; high workload to hold centreline by differential braking; potential inability to maintain track in a crosswind or on a contaminated strip.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants affected.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Effects span from a large reduction in directional-control margin (potential excursion) to a manageable case where differential braking and rudder retain track; the provided function definition does not establish the residual directional authority from differential braking/rudder alone or the excursion outcome on the semi-prepared strip, so the classification between Hazardous and Major cannot be grounded without that engineering input.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Erroneous nose door lock indication
fha.effAc: Lock indication is incorrect but the discrepancy is detectable to the crew (dual dissimilar sensing disagreement / take-off configuration monitor). If it falsely indicates locked while the door is not fully locked, the pressure boundary and forward structural load path may be unsound; the dissimilar sensing and config check provide a means to catch the error before dispatch/pressurisation.
fha.effCrew: Crew alerted to a lock indication disagreement; workload to resolve status on the ground before take-off using the second dissimilar sensing path and configuration check.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants affected.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Consequence hinges on whether the erroneous indication is caught by the second dissimilar sensing path and the take-off configuration monitor before pressurisation; the provided description states the two sensing means exist but does not establish coverage/independence sufficient to fix whether the detected-erroneous case reduces to increased workload (Minor) or a larger margin loss, so severity cannot be derived from the stated effects.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Undetected erroneous nose door lock indication
fha.effAc: Door falsely indicated locked with the discrepancy undetected: aircraft dispatched and pressurised with the nose visor not fully locked. The visor forms the pressure boundary and the forward fuselage structural load path and is a single load path treated as structure; in-flight loss of the door under pressure differential would breach the pressure boundary and the forward structural load path.
fha.effCrew: Crew continue normal duties with no alert; take no action regarding the unlocked door because it is falsely indicated locked and the error is undetected.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants affected.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Undetected false 'locked' indication permits pressurised flight with the visor unlocked; the door is the pressure boundary and a single forward-fuselage structural load path treated as structure, so its in-flight loss is a potential loss of the airplane. Assumes the door-integrity consequence stated in the SDD; pending structural/PRA substantiation. [anchor CAT-1 — Catastrophic] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Partial loss of nose door latching and locking
fha.effAc: A subset of the twelve latches or eight locking pins fails to engage while the remainder hold. Reduced margin in the door latching/locking that secures the pressure boundary and forward structural load path; the pressure interlock and remaining latches/pins provide residual retention, but the safe-flight margin of a single-load-path structural door is reduced.
fha.effCrew: Crew aware through lock status indication on the flight deck and take-off configuration check; workload to assess partial engagement and disposition before dispatch/pressurisation.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants affected.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — The number of latches/pins that may be lost while retention remains adequate, and the resulting margin against door loss under differential pressure, are structural/quantitative determinations not established by the provided function definition; without the residual-retention basis the reduction in safety margin cannot be graded between Major and Hazardous.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Undetected partial loss of nose door latching and locking
fha.effAc: A subset of the twelve latches / eight pins is not engaged with the door otherwise apparently closed, reducing retention margin of the pressure boundary and forward structural load path (SDD 5.7.1/5.7.2). Undetected, the reduced retention is a latent condition available to combine with a subsequent event.
fha.effCrew: Undetected: both lock-sensing paths (proximity harness and mechanical indicator, SDD 5.7.2) fail to reveal the shortfall, so the crew continue normally and take no action.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no passengers (SDD 1.1).
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — This is a significant-latent-failure candidate (14CFR-25.4): an undetected partial loss that could, in combination with a further failure or a pressurisation/structural event, contribute to a hazardous or catastrophic outcome. The SDD gives the retained-latch/pin count but does not state the aircraft-level consequence of a specific undetected partial-engagement level (residual retention margin, differential and structural capability of the reduced set). Effect chain not groundable to a single class — severity left empty pending structural/pressure substantiation.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Erroneous restraint tension indication
fha.effAc: The tension monitoring loop instruments every strap and annunciates loss (SDD 5.8.2). Erroneous indication misrepresents actual restraint state — either masking a real loss of tension or falsely indicating one. Masking removes the annunciation on which the crew's assessment of restraint integrity depends.
fha.effCrew: In flight the crew has indication only and no in-flight adjustment of restraint (SDD 5.8.6); erroneous indication leads to a wrong assessment of restraint status or an unnecessary diversion/attention on a false alarm.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no passengers (SDD 1.1).
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — The SDD states restraint is indication-only in flight and that the loop annunciates tension loss, but does not state the aircraft-level consequence when the indication is erroneous — in particular whether a masked loss of restraint of the 72.6 t blade produces a CG/structural effect. Consequence of erroneous indication on aircraft controllability/structure is not grounded; severity left empty pending that effect substantiation.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Partial loss of longitudinal payload restraint — within limits
fha.effAc: Loss of a single strap is carried by its neighbours — load paths are sized such that the loss of any one strap is carried by its neighbours (SDD 5.8.3). Restraint of the 72.6 t blade is maintained at reduced margin; single-strap loss is annunciated in flight (SDD 5.8.2).
fha.effCrew: Loss of tension on any strap is annunciated in flight (SDD 5.8.2); crew has indication only, no in-flight adjustment (SDD 5.8.6).
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no passengers (SDD 1.1).
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — SDD states the neighbouring straps carry a single lost strap, i.e. restraint is maintained, but does not quantify the resulting reduction in restraint margin or its aircraft-level effect (CG/structural). A benign class cannot be reached for the blade payload without that margin substantiation; severity left empty rather than defaulting to the benign end.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of longitudinal payload restraint
fha.phases: Taxi, Climb, Cruise, Descent, Approach, Landing
fha.effAc: Longitudinal restraint of the single blade is lost; under longitudinal acceleration (rejected take-off, deceleration, turbulence, manoeuvre) the blade is free to translate along the 108 m hold, producing large uncontrolled centre-of-gravity excursions beyond controllable limits and potential structural overload of the hold floor and pressure boundary.
fha.effCrew: Restraint condition is annunciated; crew cannot arrest an in-flight blade movement (no in-flight adjustment of restraint) and face a rapidly diverging CG they cannot compensate.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Uncontrolled movement of a 72.6 t blade produces CG excursions beyond controllable limits and potential loss of the airplane. [anchor CAT-1 — Catastrophic] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Undetected loss of longitudinal payload restraint
fha.phases: Taxi, Climb, Cruise, Descent, Approach, Landing
fha.effAc: Longitudinal restraint is lost but not detected; the crew continue normally while the blade is free to translate under longitudinal acceleration, driving uncontrolled CG excursions and hold-floor/pressure-boundary overload with no crew mitigation.
fha.effCrew: Crew continue their duties normally and take no action; the first cue is the aircraft response to a shifting blade, by which point the CG excursion may be uncontrollable.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Undetected loss allows an unarrested 72.6 t blade movement and CG excursion beyond controllable limits, with loss of the airplane; absence of detection removes any crew mitigation. [anchor CAT-1 — Catastrophic] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Erroneous cabin pressurisation control
fha.effAc: Pressurisation is controlled to an erroneous schedule, driving flight-deck cabin altitude away from its intended value; excursion toward higher-than-intended differential is limited by independent mechanical relief, and toward loss of pressure by loss of differential across the fuselage.
fha.effCrew: Crew become aware through cabin altitude indication and alerting, don oxygen masks and select manual pressurisation / initiate descent per procedure; increased workload during the diagnosis and reconfiguration.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot ground a single severity without the frozen hold/flight-deck pressurisation schedule and cabin-altitude limits, which are preliminary in the SDD; effect on crew depends on how far cabin altitude departs before crew action and relief limit it.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Inadvertent depressurisation
fha.effAc: Pressurisation control drives an uncommanded loss of flight-deck differential; cabin altitude rises toward the ambient altitude at the flight level, the aircraft remaining controllable but requiring an emergency descent.
fha.effCrew: Crew become aware through cabin altitude alerting, don oxygen from the quick-donning masks (system sized for the diversion time at maximum operating altitude) and initiate an emergency descent; significant workload during a time-critical reconfiguration.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Severity hinges on the maximum cabin altitude reached versus crew time of useful consciousness, which depends on the not-yet-frozen pressurisation schedule and FL260 exposure; provided context supports a rapid, protected descent but does not fix the physiological margin, so severity is left for engineering judgement against the frozen schedule.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Undetected erroneous cabin pressurisation control
fha.effAc: Pressurisation is controlled to an erroneous schedule that is not detected; the flight-deck cabin altitude departs from its intended value without alerting, so no crew mitigation is applied and the excursion is bounded only by independent mechanical relief.
fha.effCrew: Crew continue their duties normally and take no action; slow or unannounced cabin altitude departure may impair crew performance before it is recognised, without the protection of timely oxygen donning.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot ground severity without the frozen cabin-altitude schedule and the alerting/detection coverage: whether an undetected excursion reaches incapacitating cabin altitude before any residual cue depends on inputs that are preliminary in the SDD.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Partial loss of cabin pressurisation control
fha.effAc: Reduced ability to hold commanded differential; cabin/hold altitude schedule degraded but pressurisation still achievable within limits by remaining controller/outflow valve.
fha.effCrew: Crew alerted to degraded pressurisation control; assumed to select manual/backup mode and manage cabin altitude, with increased monitoring workload.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupant effect in the hold.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Degraded but still-functioning pressurisation control at the low design differential, with crew management via manual/backup mode, is a significant reduction in functional capability / significant increase in crew workload rather than a large reduction. [anchor MAJ-1 — Major] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of cabin pressurisation control
fha.effAc: Loss of controlled differential; cabin/hold altitude uncontrolled up to the maximum operating altitude, with independent mechanical relief protecting structure.
fha.effCrew: Crew alerted, don quick-donning oxygen masks and initiate emergency descent to a safe altitude; large increase in workload during the descent and diversion.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupant effect in the hold.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Uncontrolled loss of pressurisation at the maximum operating altitude, mitigated by crew oxygen and emergency descent, is a large reduction in safety margins with excessive crew workload; crew oxygen is the sizing provision. [anchor HAZ-1 — Hazardous] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Erroneous air distribution to flight deck and hold
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — The provided definition does not state what erroneous distribution produces at the aircraft level (e.g. temperature, contamination, flow misdirection between flight-deck and hold zones); the aircraft/crew effect cannot be grounded from the SDD, so severity cannot be derived. Needs the failure-effect envelope (overtemperature, smoke/fume, or zone starvation) to classify.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Partial loss of flight-deck and hold air conditioning — single-pack
fha.effAc: One air cycle pack lost; single-pack operation permitted with a reduced hold conditioning schedule, remaining pack fed from either side through the cross-bleed manifold.
fha.effCrew: Crew alerted to pack loss; selects remaining pack/bleed configuration with a slight increase in workload; no immediate diversion required.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; reduced hold conditioning schedule has no occupant effect.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Single-pack operation is an explicitly permitted degraded configuration with a reduced schedule and slight crew workload increase, i.e. a slight reduction in functional capability rather than a significant one. [anchor MIN-2 — Minor] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of flight-deck and hold air conditioning
fha.effAc: Both packs lost; no conditioned air to flight deck or hold. Pressurisation may still be maintained by bleed while conditioning is lost, but flight-deck thermal/air-quality environment degrades.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Effect on the crew depends on how quickly the flight-deck environment (temperature, ventilation, humidity) becomes untenable and on the diversion time to a suitable aerodrome; the SDD does not state the flight-deck environmental envelope under total loss of conditioning, so the crew effect and therefore severity cannot be derived without that data.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Inadvertent bleed-air ice protection (wing and inlet anti-ice on without icing demand)
fha.effAc: Bleed demand to the anti-ice system reduces available pack/bleed capacity and imposes a performance penalty when protection is not required; effect on aircraft margins depends on the magnitude of the bleed draw and the flight phase.
fha.effCrew: Crew observe anti-ice status and applied performance penalty; may deselect if manual control available.
fha.effPax: None — hold unoccupied in flight; no passengers carried.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — SDD states wing anti-ice in use reduces pack capacity and applies a performance penalty, but gives no aircraft-level margin/consequence at the phase where inadvertent operation would matter; cannot derive a class without the performance/bleed-budget effect. Requires engineering data on penalty magnitude and worst phase.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Partial loss of bleed-air ice protection (reduced coverage on wings and/or engine inlets)
fha.effAc: Reduced or incomplete protection of wing leading edges and engine inlet cowls in the icing envelope; ice accretion on unprotected areas degrades aerodynamic performance and/or inlet condition.
fha.effCrew: Crew alerted to lost coverage; may exit icing conditions, alter altitude, or manage engine handling.
fha.effPax: None — hold unoccupied in flight; no passengers carried.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — The provided material defines the function (prevent/remove ice where accretion is unacceptable) but does not state the aircraft-level effect of partial accretion within the certification icing envelope; the class cannot be derived without the aerodynamic/inlet consequence and the icing exposure. Requires icing-envelope effects analysis.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Undetected loss of bleed-air ice protection (crew unaware, no annunciation of lost coverage)
fha.effAc: With the crew unaware and continuing normally, ice accretes on unprotected wing leading edges and engine inlets in the icing envelope with no mitigating action, progressively degrading aerodynamic and inlet condition.
fha.effCrew: Crew continue duties normally and take no action; the loss is not perceived.
fha.effPax: None — hold unoccupied in flight; no passengers carried.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Unaware case (crew take no action) plausibly worsens the outcome versus the annunciated partial loss, but the underlying aircraft-level effect of accretion in the icing envelope is not stated in the provided material, so no class can be derived. Requires icing-envelope accretion effects and the loss-of-detection assumption.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of bleed-air ice protection (no protection to wings or engine inlets)
fha.effAc: No protection of wing leading edges or engine inlet cowls; in the icing envelope, unchecked accretion on wings and inlets degrades aerodynamic performance and threatens engine inlet condition across affected engines.
fha.effCrew: Crew alerted; assumed to avoid or exit icing conditions in accordance with procedure.
fha.effPax: None — hold unoccupied in flight; no passengers carried.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Complete loss of both wing and inlet protection is potentially significant, but the provided material states no aircraft-level effect (loss of margin, inlet/engine consequence) for operation in the certification icing envelope; classifying would require reaching beyond the inputs. Requires the icing-envelope effects and exposure basis.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Inadvertent electrical ice protection (stabiliser/probe/windshield heating on without demand)
fha.effAc: Electrical heating of stabiliser zones, probes, static ports and windshields energised without icing demand imposes an electrical load and potential thermal exposure on unheated-condition elements; aircraft-level effect depends on load impact and element thermal tolerance.
fha.effCrew: Crew observe ice-protection status; may deselect if manual control available.
fha.effPax: None — hold unoccupied in flight; no passengers carried.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — The provided material describes the electrically heated elements and their independent supply/monitoring but states no aircraft-level consequence of inadvertent energisation (electrical-load or thermal effect); the class cannot be derived without that effect and the element thermal-tolerance data. Requires electrical-load and thermal effects assessment.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Partial loss of electrical ice protection — single zone
fha.effAc: One electrically-heated zone unprotected in icing; annunciated to crew per design ("a lost zone is annunciated").
fha.effCrew: Crew alerted to the lost zone; workload to assess and, if necessary, exit icing conditions.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupant effect.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot ground an aircraft-level effect magnitude: the six stabiliser zones, probes and windshields are independently heated and the SDD does not state which single zone is lost nor the resulting reduction in safety margin, so the effect cannot be sized without knowing the zone. Severity left empty pending which zone and the margin lost.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Undetected loss of probe and windshield heating
fha.effAc: Probes, static ports and windshields ice-vulnerable with the loss not detected; erroneous or lost air data feeding the primary displays possible in icing conditions.
fha.effCrew: Crew continue normally, unaware; may act on erroneous airspeed/altitude before cross-check with the independent standby instrument reveals the disagreement, imposing high workload.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupant effect.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Undetected loss of probe/static/windshield heating in icing can corrupt primary air data (airspeed, altitude) fed to the displays; the crew is by definition unaware and may act on misleading data before detecting the disagreement — a large reduction in safety margins with high crew workload. The independent standby instrument on the DC essential bus shares no sensor with the primaries, which is the mitigation and the reason this is proposed Hazardous rather than Catastrophic; confirm against the air-data architecture. [anchor HAZ-1 — Hazardous] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of electrical ice protection
fha.effAc: Stabiliser leading edges, probes, static ports, windshields and both ice detectors lose electrical protection; ice accretion on protected surfaces and potential corruption of air data if operation continues in icing.
fha.effCrew: Loss annunciated; crew must exit the icing envelope and monitor for air-data degradation, with increased workload.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupant effect.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Complete loss of electrical ice protection removes stabiliser, probe, static and windshield heating simultaneously; sustained flight in the icing envelope would produce a large reduction in safety margins from ice accretion and possible air-data loss. Bleed protection of wings and cowls remains available and the loss is annunciated, so exiting icing is the assumed crew action — proposed Hazardous for your confirmation against the icing certification basis. [anchor HAZ-1 — Hazardous] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Erroneous flight and navigation information
fha.effAc: Misleading flight and navigation information presented to the crew; potential deviation from intended flight path or unsafe attitude/speed if acted upon before detection.
fha.effCrew: Crew may act on erroneous data; the independent standby instrument (sharing no supply, sensor or processing with the primary displays) enables cross-check and detection, with high workload to resolve.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupant effect.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Erroneous (misleading) flight and navigation information acted upon can produce a large reduction in safety margins and excessive crew workload. The independent standby instrument that shares no supply, sensor or processing with the primaries is the mitigation supporting Hazardous rather than Catastrophic; confirm whether a common source could drive both primary channels and the standby into agreement. [anchor HAZ-1 — Hazardous] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Erroneous system information presentation
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — This condition is not present in the model FCIM for SF-016 (which lists SF-016-M "Erroneous flight and navigation information" only) and the SDD does not describe a distinct erroneous system-information mode separable from erroneous flight/nav information. No grounded aircraft effect distinguishes it, so effects and severity are left empty pending confirmation that this is a real condition and its scope.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Undetected erroneous flight and navigation information
fha.effAc: Aircraft is flown to erroneous flight/navigation information with no crew awareness that the presented data is false; the crew acts on misleading attitude/air-data/navigation, potentially commanding the aircraft outside the safe envelope or toward terrain/obstacle without any triggering cue.
fha.effCrew: Crew receive no indication the information is erroneous and continue normal duties acting on false data; recovery depends on chance cross-check against the independent standby instrument.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants other than flight crew.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Undetected misleading primary flight and navigation information, acted upon without a triggering cue, can cause loss of control or controlled flight into terrain — multiple fatalities / loss of the airplane. [anchor CAT-1 — Catastrophic] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Partial loss of flight and navigation information
fha.effAc: A subset of flight and navigation information is lost while the remainder, including the independent standby instrument, remains available; the aircraft remains controllable on the surviving displays.
fha.effCrew: Loss is annunciated and the crew reverts to remaining displays and the standby instrument that shares no supply, sensor or processing with the primaries; increased monitoring workload, particularly in approach and landing.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants other than flight crew.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Partial loss with an independent standby instrument and reversionary display capability retained is a significant reduction in functional capability and a significant increase in crew workload, not a loss of safe flight and landing. [anchor MAJ-1 — Major] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Partial loss of system information presentation
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — This failure condition ("Partial loss of system information presentation") is not present in the SF-016 FCIM for this project (SF-016 carries only TL, PL and M/M3). Without a grounded FCIM condition text distinguishing 'system information presentation' from the SF-016-PL 'flight and navigation information' condition, I cannot state a distinct aircraft effect and therefore cannot classify. Needed: a confirmed FCIM entry defining what 'system information' is lost and how it differs from the flight/nav partial-loss condition.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of flight and navigation information
fha.effAc: All primary flight and navigation presentation is lost; the aircraft continues on the independent standby attitude, airspeed and altitude instrument on the DC essential bus, with navigation capability severely reduced.
fha.effCrew: Loss is evident; crew fly on the standby instrument alone with greatly increased workload and reduced situational awareness, requiring a diversion; large reduction in functional capabilities.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants other than flight crew.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Complete loss of primary flight and navigation display with only the independent standby instrument surviving is a large reduction in functional capabilities and excessive crew workload; the standby instrument prevents it from being Catastrophic if that independence holds. [anchor HAZ-1 — Hazardous] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Erroneous crew alerting
fha.effAc: The consolidated alerting presents false, mis-prioritised or spurious alerts; the crew may respond to a non-existent condition or be distracted from a real one, with the associated procedures potentially driving an inappropriate action.
fha.effCrew: Crew workload increases from resolving conflicting or false alerts; an erroneous alert with its associated procedure can prompt an unnecessary or incorrect crew action, degrading task performance.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants other than flight crew.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Erroneous alerting is annunciated and mediated by crew judgement against actual aircraft state; it produces a significant increase in crew workload and potential for an inappropriate action, but the two independent alerting channels and cross-checkable displays bound it below Hazardous. Confirm whether a credible erroneous-alert-plus-procedure sequence could drive a Hazardous outcome (e.g. a false fire warning prompting an unwarranted engine shutdown). [anchor MAJ-2 — Major] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Inadvertent crew alerting — a nuisance alert presented with no valid underlying condition
fha.effAc: No effect on aircraft state; the aircraft continues to function normally as the alert does not correspond to a real condition.
fha.effCrew: Crew workload increased while the spurious alert is diagnosed and dismissed; risk of distraction from primary flying task and, if recurrent, of desensitisation to the alerting list.
fha.effPax: None — hold unoccupied in flight; flight crew only.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Effect depends on alert content, frequency and flight phase, none of which the SDD states; a single nuisance alert is plausibly Minor (slight workload increase) but a misleading alert commanding an unnecessary crew response could be more severe. Cannot derive a class without the alert-priority and crew-procedure content. Confirm against the worst-case spurious alert.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Partial loss of consolidated crew alerting — a subset of alerts unavailable, crew aware of the degradation
fha.effAc: Aircraft continues to function; alerting coverage reduced for the affected subset, with those conditions no longer annunciated through the consolidated list.
fha.effCrew: Crew aware of the partial alerting loss (annunciated as a degradation); increased monitoring workload to cover the lost coverage manually, and reliance on redundant channel per the two independent processing channels.
fha.effPax: None — hold unoccupied in flight.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — The aircraft effect depends entirely on which alerts are lost, which the SDD does not enumerate; a small loss with a redundant channel available is plausibly Minor/Major, but loss of a critical alert subset could be higher. Cannot derive a class without the alert-priority allocation. Confirm against the worst-case lost subset.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Erroneous fire or overheat indication (false warning or misleading location) with crew aware
fha.phases: Taxi, Climb, Cruise, Descent, Approach, Landing
fha.effAc: A false fire/overheat warning may prompt an unnecessary engine shut-down and/or extinguishant discharge, reducing available thrust or protection; a misleading location may direct the crew's response to the wrong zone.
fha.effCrew: Increased workload to diagnose and act on a warning that does not reflect a real fire; potential for an unnecessary drill (fire handle, shutdown, diversion).
fha.effPax: No occupants in the hold; flight crew only.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Unnecessary shut-down of one of four engines and/or an unnecessary drill/diversion is a significant increase in crew workload and a significant reduction in functional capability, but the aircraft continues to fly; effects do not reach a large reduction in safety margins. [anchor MAJ-2 — Major] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Partial loss of fire and overheat detection — one zone or one loop lost, annunciated (crew aware)
fha.effAc: Detection coverage of one monitored zone is degraded or lost with the loss annunciated; a subsequent fire or overheat in the affected zone may be detected late or not at all, but the crew is aware of the degradation and can apply operational limitations.
fha.effCrew: Crew is alerted to the loss of coverage and manages by procedure (increased vigilance, possible dispatch/continuation limitation); increased workload.
fha.effPax: No occupants in the hold; flight crew only.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Annunciated loss of detection coverage in one zone is a significant reduction in a safety-related functional capability with the crew aware and able to mitigate; it does not by itself reach a large reduction in safety margins. [anchor MAJ-1 — Major] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Undetected partial loss of fire and overheat detection coverage — crew unaware, continues normal duties
fha.effAc: Detection coverage of a monitored zone is degraded without annunciation; a fire or overheat in the affected zone is detected late or not at all, and extinguishing action may be delayed or omitted, allowing an uncontrolled fire to develop and spread from a fire zone.
fha.effCrew: Crew continue normal duties and take no action on the latent loss; no cue that coverage is reduced until a fire escapes detection.
fha.effPax: No occupants in the hold; flight crew only.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: A latent loss of detection coverage that, combined with a subsequent fire in an engine nacelle, APU or bleed-duct zone, leaves the fire undetected until it escalates represents a large reduction in safety margins; the latent nature is the driver and is recorded per §25.4 significant-latent-failure treatment. [anchor HAZ-1 — Hazardous] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of fire and overheat detection across all monitored zones — annunciated (crew aware)
fha.effAc: No detection available in any monitored zone (engine nacelles, APU, bleed ducts, main gear bays, hold smoke stations), annunciated; a subsequent fire or overheat anywhere is not detected by the aircraft, though the crew is aware detection is lost and can divert and apply limitations.
fha.effCrew: Crew alerted to total loss of detection; workload increased to manage by procedure (precautionary limitations, diversion); primary means of first-alerting a fire is removed.
fha.effPax: No occupants in the hold; flight crew only.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Total loss of the aircraft's fire/overheat first-detection means, with fire zones including four engine nacelles and the APU, is a large reduction in safety margins even with the crew aware, since a subsequent fire would proceed undetected; it does not by itself lose the aircraft. [anchor HAZ-1 — Hazardous] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Undetected complete loss of fire and overheat detection — crew unaware, continues normal duties
fha.effAc: All fire/overheat detection is lost without annunciation; a subsequent fire or overheat in any monitored zone — including an engine nacelle or the APU compartment — develops with no aircraft warning and no crew response, permitting an uncontrolled fire adjacent to fuel, structure and control runs.
fha.effCrew: Crew continue normal duties and take no action; the first indication of fire would be a secondary consequence (smoke, system loss, structural effect) rather than the detection system.
fha.effPax: No occupants in the hold; flight crew only.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: A latent total loss of detection, combined with a subsequent undetected and unfought fire in a fire zone containing flammable fluid adjacent to structure and control runs, can progress to loss of the airplane; the latent, unannunciated nature drives the class and is recorded as a significant latent failure per §25.4. [anchor CAT-1 — Catastrophic] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Inadvertent extinguishant discharge — a fire-extinguisher bottle discharges into a nacelle or the APU compartment with no fire present
fha.effAc: An engine-pair bottle charge is expended into a non-burning zone; the SDD provides two bottles per engine pair cross-plumbed so either bottle can serve either nacelle, so extinguishing reserve for that pair is reduced but not necessarily eliminated.
fha.effCrew: Discharge status annunciated to the crew alerting system; crew assess and manage remaining protection.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants affected.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Effect is reduced extinguishing reserve for the affected engine pair; the SDD does not state the aircraft-level consequence of a subsequent fire with the reduced reserve, so an aircraft effect sufficient to commit severity cannot be grounded. Needs the fire-hazard case and remaining-coverage judgement.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Partial loss of fire extinguishing capability — reduced extinguishing coverage in one or more fire zones (e.g. one bottle of an engine pair unavailable, or APU protection lost)
fha.effAc: Extinguishing available but degraded: a zone that would have had two-bottle or cross-plumbed coverage now has reduced agent available; dual-loop detection remains and detection is unaffected.
fha.effCrew: Crew retains fire handles and detection warnings; extinguishing remains a crew action but with reduced reserve.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants affected.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — The SDD states the redundancy (two bottles per pair, cross-plumbed, independent APU bottle) but does not state the aircraft-level outcome of a fire when only reduced extinguishing is available; without the fire-propagation / alternate-isolation case an aircraft effect cannot be grounded to commit severity.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of fire extinguishing capability — no means to extinguish or suppress fire in the engine and APU fire zones
fha.effAc: A detected nacelle or APU fire cannot be extinguished by the fixed system; engine shut-off and fire-handle fuel isolation remain available as means to remove the fire source, but active suppression is lost.
fha.effCrew: Crew receives fire warning and can pull the fire handle to isolate fuel and shut down the affected engine/APU, but cannot discharge extinguishant.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants affected.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — The SDD does not state the aircraft-level consequence of an unextinguished nacelle or APU fire (propagation to structure, adjacent systems or fuel), nor whether fuel isolation alone bounds it. Committing severity requires the fire-hazard case; effects are stated but severity cannot be derived here.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Inadvertent overboard discharge of oxygen — a crew-oxygen cylinder overpressure vents overboard, depleting stored oxygen
fha.effAc: Overboard discharge shown by the fuselage-skin thermal discharge indicator; stored crew oxygen is reduced or lost depending on crossover state, reducing the reserve available for a subsequent depressurisation or smoke/fume event.
fha.effCrew: Crew has cylinder pressure and low-pressure alerting on the flight deck; can use the crossover to draw on the remaining cylinder if intact.
fha.effPax: No passenger oxygen fitted; hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants affected.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Effect is reduced or lost crew-oxygen reserve; the SDD does not tie this to a specific depressurisation/diversion aircraft effect, and either cylinder can supply the crew at reduced reserve, so the aircraft-level outcome cannot be grounded to commit severity..
