Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Partial loss of crew breathing oxygen supply — reduced oxygen quantity or a single cylinder/regulator unavailable
fha.effAc: Breathing oxygen remains available but at reduced reserve: with one cylinder lost the crossover permits the other cylinder to supply the crew at reduced reserve; regulators are independent per mask so a single regulator loss affects one station only.
fha.effCrew: Crew retains breathing oxygen for donning on a pressurisation, smoke or fume event, but with reduced endurance margin for the diversion; cylinder pressure displayed continuously.
fha.effPax: No passenger oxygen fitted; hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants affected.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — The system is sized for four occupants with reserve and either cylinder can supply the crew at reduced reserve; the SDD does not state the aircraft effect of the reduced reserve against the diversion/altitude case, so severity cannot be derived without that reserve-versus-diversion judgement.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of crew breathing oxygen supply
fha.effAc: No direct effect on aircraft controllability; the aircraft remains flyable. Consequence is realised only in combination with a pressurisation loss, smoke or fume event, where the crew has no breathing-oxygen protection for the required emergency descent and diversion.
fha.effCrew: Flight crew (crew-only aircraft, hold unoccupied) have no breathing oxygen for a depressurisation, smoke or fume event; risk of hypoxia or fume incapacitation during descent and diversion, impairing or preventing safe conduct of the emergency.
fha.effPax: No passengers carried; hold is not occupied in flight.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Loss of the sole crew-oxygen means removes flight-crew protection during a depressurisation/smoke/fume descent, credibly producing crew impairment/incapacitation that impairs task performance during the emergency. [anchor HAZ-2 — Hazardous] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Undetected partial loss of crew breathing oxygen supply
fha.effCrew: Reduced breathing-oxygen capability with the crew unaware; on a depressurisation/smoke/fume event the available protection time is shorter than the crew assumes.
fha.effPax: No passengers carried; hold is not occupied in flight.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot derive a class: the SDD does not quantify how much reserve is lost in the partial case, the diversion/descent duration the oxygen must cover, or the resulting aircraft-level effect; classifying would require guessing the shortfall against the required duration.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Partial loss of ground deceleration
fha.effAc: Reduced braking capability lengthens the landing/RTO rollout; against the 1,800 m semi-prepared requirement and ~1,080 m predicted rollout the margin is eroded but braking remains available from remaining sources (dual hydraulic supply plus accumulator reserve).
fha.effCrew: Crew detects longer deceleration and applies remaining braking / reverse thrust; increased workload managing the stop on a semi-prepared surface.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied; no occupant effect.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Significant reduction in landing/RTO safety margin on a semi-prepared strip with degraded but available braking; effects support MAJ-1. [anchor MAJ-1 — Major] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Undetected partial loss of ground deceleration
fha.effAc: Degraded braking not annunciated; crew initiates the stop expecting full deceleration and the reduced capability manifests as an unexpectedly long rollout, consuming the margin between the 1,800 m requirement and ~1,080 m predicted rollout with no time to compensate, risking overrun on the semi-prepared strip.
fha.effCrew: No warning; crew continues normal procedure and discovers the shortfall late in the rollout with limited remaining stopping distance.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied; no occupant effect.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Latent degradation removes the crew's opportunity to compensate early, driving toward runway overrun on a short semi-prepared surface; large reduction in safety margin supports HAZ-1. [anchor HAZ-1 — Hazardous] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of ground deceleration
fha.effAc: No wheel braking available; deceleration relies only on reverse thrust (inboard engines) and aerodynamic drag, insufficient to stop within the 1,800 m semi-prepared distance against ~1,080 m nominal rollout, leading to high probability of runway overrun.
fha.effCrew: Crew applies all remaining deceleration means under high workload; unable to arrest the aircraft within available distance.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied; no occupant effect.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Total loss of braking on a short semi-prepared strip drives runway overrun with the aircraft on its gear; large reduction in functional capability and safety margin supports HAZ-1. Whether the overrun is survivable determines any escalation to Catastrophic — leave to engineering judgement. [anchor HAZ-1 — Hazardous] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of nose door latching and locking
fha.effAc: With no latch or lock engagement the nose visor is not retained; the door forms part of the pressure boundary and the forward fuselage structural load path when closed (SDD 5.7.1). In flight, loss of retention permits door movement/opening against pressurisation differential, loss of the pressure boundary and loss of the forward structural load path.
fha.effCrew: Lock status is displayed on the flight deck and included in the take-off configuration check (SDD 5.7.6); on the ground the condition is detectable pre-flight. In flight the crew cannot reclose or relatch (door cannot be operated in flight, SDD 5.7.6).
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no passengers (SDD 1.1).
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Door is the pressure boundary and forward fuselage structural load path when closed (SDD 5.7.1/5.7.3); in-flight loss of latching and locking permits loss of pressure boundary and forward structural load path — potential loss of the airplane. Effects drive CAT-1; confirm. [anchor CAT-1 — Catastrophic] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Partial loss of longitudinal payload restraint — two adjacent stations
fha.effAc: Loss of restraint at two adjacent stations — annunciated as a restraint condition requiring immediate attention (SDD 5.8.2). The single-strap load-sharing argument (SDD 5.8.3) is not stated to cover two adjacent stations, so longitudinal restraint margin of the 72.6 t blade at those stations may be substantially reduced, risking blade shift and consequent CG/structural effect.
fha.effCrew: Annunciated as a restraint condition requiring immediate attention (SDD 5.8.2); crew has indication only and cannot adjust restraint in flight (SDD 5.8.6).
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no passengers (SDD 1.1).
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: SDD substantiates neighbour load-sharing only for a single strap and flags two adjacent stations as requiring immediate attention (SDD 5.8.2/5.8.3); loss over two adjacent stations of a 72.6 t single-item restraint threatens a large reduction in restraint capability with potential blade shift — proposed HAZ-1. Requires structural substantiation of the two-adjacent-station load case; confirm. [anchor HAZ-1 — Hazardous] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Undetected suppression of a valid alert — a genuine underlying condition exists but its alert is suppressed and the crew is unaware
fha.effAc: The underlying (potentially safety-significant) condition progresses without crew mitigation; aircraft effect is that of the un-annunciated condition allowed to develop unchecked.
fha.effCrew: Crew continue duties normally and take no action on the suppressed condition; the alerting system is the primary means of knowing what has failed, so its silent suppression removes the trigger for the required procedure.
fha.effPax: None — hold unoccupied in flight.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Silent suppression of a valid alert is a latent failure that defeats the crew's primary means of detecting and mitigating an underlying condition; combined with a further failure it drives toward the severity of that un-annunciated condition. Proposed Hazardous as a latent alerting-integrity loss (HAZ-1). CONFIRM: could be Catastrophic if the suppressed alert is the sole warning for a Catastrophic underlying condition — reclassify against the worst-case masked condition. [anchor HAZ-1 — Hazardous] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of consolidated crew alerting — no alerts presented, crew aware alerting is lost
fha.effAc: No consolidated annunciation of any system condition; the aircraft continues to fly but the crew's single prioritised means of knowing what has failed is gone.
fha.effCrew: Crew aware the alerting list is unavailable (annunciated loss); significantly increased workload to monitor every system's raw status directly and identify conditions without prioritised alerting or associated procedures.
fha.effPax: None — hold unoccupied in flight.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: With crew aware of the total alerting loss, the effect is a significant increase in crew workload and a significant reduction in the means to detect subsequent conditions (MAJ-1/MAJ-2). Proposed Major for the AWARE case. CONFIRM: the workload↔severity judgement and whether raw system indications remain adequate depend on flight-deck design detail not in the SDD. [anchor MAJ-2 — Major] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Undetected complete loss of consolidated crew alerting — alerting is entirely unavailable and the crew is unaware of the loss
fha.effAc: No condition on any system is annunciated and no failure of the alerting itself is indicated; any subsequently developing condition progresses with no crew trigger to mitigate it.
fha.effCrew: Crew continue duties normally, believing the alerting list is functioning; they receive no warning of any condition that arises, removing the trigger for every associated procedure.
fha.effPax: None — hold unoccupied in flight.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: A latent total loss of the crew's primary failure-annunciation means: no alert of any subsequent condition and no indication that alerting itself is lost. Proposed Hazardous (HAZ-1) as a latent large reduction in the means to detect and respond to failures. CONFIRM: approaches Catastrophic if a Catastrophic-tending condition could develop wholly unannunciated — reclassify against the worst-case masked condition and confirm the loss is truly undetectable. [anchor HAZ-1 — Hazardous] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Erroneous ground deceleration — braking applied incorrectly (wrong distribution, spurious or asymmetric application) during the ground roll
fha.effAc: Erroneous braking distribution produces an asymmetric decelerating force and a yawing moment during the ground roll; on the semi-prepared strip with limited rollout margin (~1,080 m predicted against 1,800 m required) the aircraft departs the intended ground track, risking runway/strip excursion.
fha.effCrew: Crew must detect the heading departure from track and directional cues and counter with steering/rudder and thrust; workload is high during a time-critical high-energy ground phase.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; crew only aboard. Injury risk arises from a strip excursion rather than the braking event itself.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Asymmetric erroneous braking on a low-friction semi-prepared surface with limited stopping margin yields a large reduction in directional-control safety margin and excessive crew workload during a high-energy ground phase; effects support Hazardous. Awareness assumed via heading/track cues — confirm whether a crew-unaware variant is warranted. [anchor HAZ-1 — Hazardous] — engineer to confirm.

assumptions.text: The four resource-typed systems (FUE, HYD, EPS, EWS) are captured in the Resources model and are not authored as aircraft functions.
assumptions.rationale: The house modeling rule forbids authoring resources as functions; the SDD independently types these four systems as resources supplying other systems.
assumptions.ifWrong: If any resource must be modeled as a consumed function, the function list would gain provide-power/provide-fuel rows, which this rule prohibits.
assumptions.usedFor: Exclusion of FUE, HYD, EPS, EWS from the add_function set.

citations.quote: Four are treated as resources — they exist to supply other systems rather than to act on the aircraft themselves

assumptions.text: The nose door load path and the hold floor hard points are structure and are excluded from functional decomposition.
assumptions.rationale: The modeling rule excludes structural integrity from functional-FHA items; the SDD explicitly treats both as structure.
assumptions.ifWrong: If treated functionally these would add structural-integrity 'functions', which the FUNCTION vs STRUCTURE rule prohibits.
assumptions.usedFor: Exclusion of NZD door structure and CRG hard points from sub-functions.

citations.quote: the door is a single load path and is treated as structure

assumptions.text: Top-function names group multiple SDD systems' behaviours (e.g. FCS surfaces under 'Control aircraft trajectory') at aircraft level.
assumptions.rationale: The SDD is organised by system, not by aircraft function, so aircraft-level top-function grouping is a derivation the engineer must confirm.
assumptions.ifWrong: If the intended top-function boundary differs, sub-functions would regroup under different parents though the sub-function content is unchanged.
assumptions.usedFor: funcName grouping across all 21 add_function actions.

citations.quote: It does not tell you what the aircraft-level functions are

assumptions.text: Erroneous / uncommanded roll, pitch and yaw responses can develop below crew detection thresholds, justifying a crew-Unaware row for each primary axis.
assumptions.rationale: The SDD describes annunciation of degraded laws and jam/asymmetry discretes but does not establish a per-condition detection threshold, so the undetected-onset variant cannot be dismissed.
assumptions.ifWrong: If all axis malfunctions are self-evident or always annunciated, the three crew-Unaware rows (SF-003/004/005) collapse and only the Aware rows remain.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-003 Unaware, SF-004 Unaware, SF-005 Unaware rows

citations.quote: Degraded laws are annunciated.

praData.threat: Tire burst / flailing tread — main gear
praData.desc: Burst of one or more of the twenty tyres (six three-wheel main bogies) releasing debris and flailing tread within the main gear bays. Debris size/energy/trajectory not yet defined — retained for substantiation.
praData.systems: LDG, HYD (brake lines A and B), FCS steering/brake harnesses
praData.csfl: Brake hydraulic lines for systems A and B run through each main gear bay in adjacent, separately-clipped bundles — a single burst event in a bay is a common cause challenging both brake supplies to that bogie group, defeating the nominal A/B brake independence locally.
praData.mitigation:
Brake lines A and B separately clipped and shielded within each bay; dual hydraulic supply to brakes plus accumulator reserve sized to six full brake applications; steering and braking electrical harnesses routed on opposite sides of each bay. Adequacy of the shared-bay separation to survive tyre debris to be SHOWN ACCEPTABLE (open).
Proposed requirements: • The main gear bay installation shall protect brake hydraulic lines A and B such that a single tyre-burst debris event cannot cause loss of both brake supplies to the affected bogie group.
aiRequirements: The main gear bay installation shall protect brake hydraulic lines A and B such that a single tyre-burst debris event cannot cause loss of both brake supplies to the affected bogie group.

praData.desc: Bird strike into one of the four podded engine inlets beneath the high wing, per §25.571(e)(1)/§25.631/§33.76. Bird size and multiple-ingestion case to be defined against the type-design threat.
praData.mitigation: Left and right engine pairs sit in separate zones; services to each engine routed through the corresponding pylon and not commingled outboard of the wing root — a single strike is confined to one engine. Continued flight after loss of any one engine at or after V1 is a stated design case (survivability MINIMISED to single-engine loss).

praData.threat: Bird strike — forward fuselage, windshields and probes
praData.desc: Bird strike on forward-facing structure: nose visor (zone 110), flight-deck windshields (130), and the pitot/static/AoA probes and the two forward-fuselage ice detectors. Impact energy/trajectory to be defined against the type-design bird threat.
praData.csfl: The two ice detectors are of the same type and installed on opposite sides of the forward fuselage; their commonality is a recorded item — a strike geometry defeating both is a potential common cause for loss of ice detection.
praData.mitigation: Ice detection is advisory with manual selection available at any time; probes/static/windshields are electrically heated and monitored individually; standby instrument shares no supply/sensor/processing with the primaries. Adequacy of forward-facing structure and the two same-type detectors against the bird threat to be SHOWN ACCEPTABLE (open).

praData.threat: Lightning strike (§25.1316, AC 20-136B) — direct attachment and indirect transient coupling into aircraft electrical/electronic systems
affectedZones: 530 / 540 (wing root — HV feeder transit, bleed duct penetration)
800 (aft fuselage and empennage — rudder runs, stabiliser heater feeders, APU)
praData.desc: Direct lightning attachment at extremities (nose visor, wing tips, empennage, engine nacelles) with conducted/coupled transients propagating along the six EWS routes (HV feeder L/R, LV signal L/R, data channels 1/2). The transient can couple simultaneously into multiple fly-by-wire flight-control computers, the air-data/inertial reference units and the FADEC channels — the nominal FCS independence (three dissimilar computers on three sources) is an electrical-separation claim that a coupled transient can defeat. Survivability turns on transient control at bundle/box level and on the standby instrument, which the SDD states shares no supply, sensor or processing with the primaries.
praData.systems: FCS, AVI, EPS, EWS, PRP (FADEC), IPS (stabiliser heater feeders), NZD (lock sensing harness)
praData.csfl: Coincident lightning transient coupling into all three flight control computers (SF-004-TL / SF-003-TL / SF-005-TL) and/or all three air-data/inertial reference units driving SF-016-M3 — common-cause defeat of the FCS and display redundancy that the fault trees treat as independent
praData.mitigation:
Proposed requirements: • The aircraft structure and its lightning attachment/exit zones shall be protected against catastrophic direct and indirect effects of lightning per §25.1316 and AC 20-136B, such that no single strike defeats the independence of the three flight control computers or the three air-data/inertial reference units.
• The integrated standby instrument on the DC essential bus shall be shown to survive the lightning indirect-effects environment independently of the primary display feeders, preserving a survivable attitude/airspeed/altitude source.
aiFunctions: SF-016 Acquire and present flight, navigation and system information
aiRequirements: The aircraft structure and its lightning attachment/exit zones shall be protected against catastrophic direct and indirect effects of lightning per §25.1316 and AC 20-136B, such that no single strike defeats the independence of the three flight control computers or the three air-data/inertial reference units.

The integrated standby instrument on the DC essential bus shall be shown to survive the lightning indirect-effects environment independently of the primary display feeders, preserving a survivable attitude/airspeed/altitude source.

praData.threat: High-Intensity Radiated Fields (§25.1317, AC 20-158A) — external RF illumination coupling into aircraft electrical/electronic systems
affectedZones: 120 / 300 / 400 (equipment bays — FCC 1/2/3, avionics racks, reference units)
200 / 300 / 400 (hold — LV signal route, data network, restraint tension loop)
praData.desc: External RF fields couple into wiring and equipment through apertures and along the six EWS routes, illuminating the fly-by-wire flight-control computers, the three air-data/inertial reference units, the display processing units, the dual data network and the FADEC channels simultaneously. HIRF is a whole-aircraft field, so the FCS and AVI independence claims (three dissimilar computers on three sources; dual networks on opposite sides) are exposed to a common-mode upset unless equipment-level and bundle-level RF protection is substantiated. The standby instrument, wired directly to the DC essential bus on an independent route, is the survivable reference to be protected.

praData.csfl: Simultaneous HIRF upset of all three flight control computers (SF-004-TL / SF-003-TL / SF-005-TL) and/or all three air-data/inertial reference units feeding SF-016-M3 — common-mode defeat of redundancy that the fault trees model as independent electrical/processing channels

praData.threat: Hail / ice impact on forward-facing structure and engine inlets (§25.571(e)(2))
praData.desc: Hail impact on forward-facing surfaces: nose visor structure (zone 110), wing leading edges (510/520), engine inlet cowls and ingestion into the four turbofans (nacelle zones 610–640), and flight-deck windshields / pitot-static / AoA / ice-detector heads on the forward fuselage. Model: impact energy of the certification hail on structure, transparencies and probes plus ingestion into the inboard/outboard inlets. Survivability question is whether the aircraft retains thrust, structure and flight/nav sensing after a hail encounter, not how often one occurs.
praData.systems: PRP, FCS structure (nose visor NZD), AVI (air data / windshields / ice detectors), IPS (ice detector heads)
praData.csfl: Common environmental cause across all four engine inlets simultaneously (all in the hail cloud) and across both forward air-data / windshield installations — defeats the per-engine and per-channel independence otherwise claimed for PRP and AVI. Both ice detectors are of the same type on opposite sides of the forward fuselage, so a common hail/ice environment can degrade both.
praData.mitigation:
Windshield / transparency and forward structure sized to the certification hail impact; engine inlet and fan hail-ingestion substantiation per the engine type; probe and ice-detector heads qualified for impact and de-iced. Retain as PRA survivability items pending impact test / analysis — acceptability not yet demonstrated.
Proposed requirements: • The forward-facing structure (nose visor, windshields, leading edges) shall withstand the certification-basis hail impact without loss of structural integrity or pressure boundary.
• The four engine inlets and fans shall tolerate certification-basis hail ingestion without a hazardous loss of thrust across more than one engine.
• The pitot-static, angle-of-attack and ice-detector installations shall retain function after certification-basis hail impact, or an undetected-erroneous flight/navigation information condition shall be precluded.

praData.threat: Icing / ice accretion and ice shedding (§25.1419, AC 20-73A)
praData.desc: Ice accretion on unprotected or under-protected surfaces, probes, static ports, windshields and inlets, and ice shedding into engine inlets. Model: accretion in the icing envelope of the certification basis defeating or overrunning the bleed-air wing/cowl protection (zones 510/520, 610–640), the electrically heated stabiliser zones (zone 800) and the electrically heated probes/windshields/ice-detectors on the forward fuselage (zone 130). Ice shed from wing or forward structure ingested by the inboard engines. Survivability question is whether protection, sensing and thrust survive the icing encounter.
praData.systems: IPS, PRP (inlet anti-ice / shed ingestion), AVI (probe / windshield / ice-detector heating), ECS (shares the bleed manifold with IPS)
praData.csfl: The two ice detectors are identical in type — a common environmental icing condition that masks detection on one can mask both, defeating the independence of ice detection. Wing and inlet bleed protection draws from the same cross-bleed manifold that feeds the ECS packs, so a bleed-manifold event is common-cause across IPS and ECS. Loss of probe/windshield heating is a common cause across the air-data sources feeding SF-016.
praData.mitigation:
Bleed-air wing/cowl anti-ice from either side through the cross-bleed manifold; six independently supplied electrical stabiliser zones with lost-zone annunciation; individually monitored probe/windshield/ice-detector heating; two ice detectors with automatic activation. Common-type ice-detector commonality and the shared bleed manifold retained as PRA/CMA items to substantiate — acceptability not yet demonstrated.
Proposed requirements: • The ice protection system shall protect the surfaces, inlets and probes required by the certification icing envelope such that no undetected loss of protection occurs.
• Loss of probe and windshield heating in icing shall not produce an undetected erroneous flight and navigation information condition.
• Ice shed from the wing or forward structure shall not cause a hazardous loss of thrust on more than one engine.

praData.threat: Cabin/hold fire and smoke (in-flight fire in the unoccupied hold, an equipment bay or the flight deck; smoke/fume propagation)
praData.desc: Fire or overheat originating in the hold (stations 1-9), a hold equipment bay (mid bay houses FCC 2, aft bay houses FCC 3), the forward equipment bay (FCC 1, crew oxygen cylinders), the flight deck, or the aft-fuselage/APU compartment. The hold carries smoke detection at nine stations and NO suppression — a recorded design decision to be substantiated (SDD §5.12.2). Smoke/fume can reach the flight deck and equipment bays along the full-length low-voltage / data routes and the left-side electrical route that share the hold zones. Crew oxygen masks are quick-donning full-face with smoke goggles (SDD §5.13.2).
praData.systems: FPR, CRG, AVI, FCS, OXY, ECS, EPS, EWS
praData.csfl: A fire/overheat in the mid or aft hold co-locates with FCC 2 (zone 300) and FCC 3 (zone 400); loss or corruption of two of the three dissimilar flight-control computers by a single in-zone fire challenges the three-computer independence claim. Hold detection is present but no suppression is fitted, so an in-hold fire is not extinguished by aircraft means. Smoke reaching the flight deck via shared LV/data routes can degrade crew information and alerting simultaneously.
praData.mitigation:
Substantiate the no-hold-suppression decision (SDD §5.12.2) as an explicit acceptability case per §25.855. Maintain physical separation of FCC 2 (zone 300) and FCC 3 (zone 400) from hold fire load paths so a single hold fire cannot take two computers. Nine-station hold smoke detection provides crew annunciation; crew smoke goggles / full-face masks (OXY) preserve crew function during smoke. Dual-loop detection with separated routing in the nacelle/APU/bleed-duct/gear-bay zones (SDD §5.12.2/§5.12.5). Discharge circuits on the hot battery bus remain available with all generation lost (SDD §5.12.5).
Proposed requirements: • The hold fire protection installation shall be shown to comply with §25.855 for the carriage of a single unitised blade with detection and no suppression, substantiating the recorded no-suppression decision.
• The installation shall preserve separation of the three dissimilar flight control computers such that a single fire in one hold zone cannot render more than one flight control computer inoperative.
• Smoke/fume propagation from the hold to the flight deck along shared low-voltage and data routes shall be controlled such that crew flight and navigation information and consolidated crew alerting remain available.

SF-019 Extinguish engine and APU fire
SF-020 Supply breathing oxygen to the flight crew

zsaData.desc: Nose visor structure — unpressurised when open, forms pressure boundary and forward structural load path when closed. Nose door lock sensing harness originates here (routes 110→120→130).
zsaData.equip: Visor latches (12 rotary on common torque shaft), lock pins (8, separate actuator/supply), lock actuator, proximity sensing harness
zsaData.interference: Common torque shaft drives all twelve latches — single mechanical common cause. Sensing harness and mechanical indicator linkage separated per §5.7.5; verify separation maintained to the two flight-deck bulkhead penetrations.
zsaData.mitigation: Confirm two dissimilar independently-routed lock-sensing paths (proximity harness vs mechanical linkage) remain separated through zone; confirm pressure interlock (residual <0.1 psi) integrity; inspect torque-shaft common-cause exposure. Item flagged in SDD for particular-risk/zonal attention.

zsaData.desc: Forward equipment bay — pressurised, conditioned. Houses FCC 1 (one of three separated flight-control-computer bays), crew oxygen cylinders, forward avionics racks. LV signal and data channel routes originate/transit here.
zsaData.equip: FCC 1, oxygen cylinders (2 HP gaseous), forward avionics racks
zsaData.interference: Oxygen cylinders (high-pressure, oxidiser) co-located with avionics racks and FCC 1. SDD §5.13.5 states cylinders are outside any zone containing a high-energy electrical source — verify against forward avionics rack energy levels in this bay.
zsaData.mitigation: Confirm O2 cylinder installation separation from electrical energy sources and routing of O2 supply line clear of HV feeder; confirm FCC 1 bay separation from FCC 2/3 preserves the three-computer independence claim; materials compatibility check around oxygen.

zsaData.desc: Flight deck — pressurised, occupied. Houses primary displays, inceptors, independent standby instrument, fire handles, crew oxygen masks. Nose door lock sensing terminates here at two separated bulkhead penetrations.
zsaData.equip: Display units, inceptors, integrated standby instrument, fire handles, crew oxygen masks
zsaData.interference: Standby instrument shares no supply/sensor/processing with primary displays (§5.11.3) — verify physical routing in this zone preserves that independence. Fire handles and O2 masks are crew-critical hardware in an occupied zone.
zsaData.mitigation: Confirm standby-instrument wiring on route independent of primary display feeders; confirm crew-oxygen mask stations and fire-handle runs protected; workload/reach ergonomics for two-crew nominal complement (HIDH, general applicability — reference only).

zsaData.desc: Forward hold (stations 1–3) — low differential, unoccupied. Houses saddles 1–3, restraint straps, tension loop, smoke detectors. HV feeder, LV signal, data channels, HYD C run, and restraint tension loop all transit.
zsaData.equip: Saddles 1–3, restraint straps + electric winches, restraint tension monitoring loop, smoke detectors (part of 9-station hold set)
zsaData.interference: Restraint tension monitoring loop shares hold zone with the fuel gallery vent and the left-side electrical route (§5.8.5, recorded item). Single instrumented loop — no redundancy in restraint monitoring coverage. Hold has smoke detection but NO suppression (§5.12.2).
zsaData.mitigation: Assess loop co-location with fuel vent + electrical route for common-cause; substantiate the no-hold-suppression decision (recorded SDD assumption); verify saddle hard-point attachment; inspect winch electrical routing. Cross-link to Cabin/hold fire PRA-99256.

zsaData.desc: Mid hold (stations 4–6) — low differential, unoccupied. Houses saddles 4–6, mid equipment bay, FCC 2, and the HV/LV crossing points. Convergence zone: fuel gallery, HYD A/B wing-root run, HYD C, brake lines A/B, HV feeders L/R, LV signal, data channels 1/2, bleed cross-bleed manifold all transit.
zsaData.equip: Saddles 4–6, FCC 2, mid equipment bay, HV↔LV crossing points (x2), cross-bleed manifold
zsaData.interference: Highest-density convergence zone on the aircraft. HV feeder × LV signal cross at two identified points here (§5.5.5, §5.14.2) — the only two crossings, shielding replaces separation. HYD A+B share wing-root run through this region. Cross-bleed manifold joins both bleed sides here. FCC 2 independence from FCC 1/3 must survive this convergence.
zsaData.mitigation: Verify HV/LV crossing-point shielding and minimum distance; test HYD A/B shared-run independence claim (CMA candidate — every AND-gate claim relying on A/B independence); confirm FCC 2 separation; confirm fuel gallery separation from hydraulic and HV routes (§5.2.5). Multiple CMA/PRA cross-links.

zsaData.desc: Aft hold (stations 7–9) — low differential, unoccupied. Houses saddles 7–9, aft equipment bay, FCC 3. HYD C run, LV signal, data channels, restraint tension loop transit.
zsaData.interference: FCC 3 is the third of the three separated flight-control-computer bays — its independence from FCC 1 (120) and FCC 2 (300) is the basis of the three-computer voting redundancy. Restraint tension loop continues through this zone.
zsaData.mitigation: Confirm FCC 3 bay separation and power source dissimilarity preserved; verify aft saddle hard-points; inspect restraint loop continuity and separation from HYD C run.

zsaData.desc: Left wing box and leading edge (mirrored by 520 right) — flammable fluid present. Houses fuel tanks, cross-feed gallery, wing anti-ice ducting, outboard electrical route. Fuel feed gallery and wing anti-ice ducting transit.
zsaData.equip: Integral fuel tanks (outboard/mid), cross-feed gallery segment, wing anti-ice piccolo ducting, outboard electrical route
zsaData.interference: Wing anti-ice ducting (hot bleed) shares the leading edge with the outboard electrical route, separated by a shielded partition along the full run (§5.10.5). Flammable-fluid zone with a hot pneumatic source and an electrical source in proximity — ignition-source management is the governing installation concern.
zsaData.mitigation: Verify shielded partition integrity full-length between anti-ice duct and electrical route; confirm fuel tank vent/surge lines routed outboard of all electrical harnesses (§5.2.5); ignition-source separation and bonding. Cross-link Lightning (§25.1316) and Ice PRAs; fuel-tank flammability per §25.981.

zsaData.desc: Left wing root (mirrored by 540 right) — pressure boundary transit. Houses HYD A and B wing-root run, bleed duct penetration, HV feeder transit. HYD A/B wing-root run, HV feeder, bleed ducts transit.
zsaData.equip: HYD A wing-root run, HYD B wing-root run, bleed duct penetration, HV feeder
zsaData.interference: HYD systems A and B share this wing-root run where both cross the pressure boundary (§5.4.5, §5.3.5) — SDD itself records this as an independence claim to be tested, not assumed. A single physical event here could defeat both A and B. Bleed duct and HV feeder also transit.
zsaData.mitigation: Common-mode analysis of the HYD A/B shared run — this coupling must be reflected as a common-cause contributor in any fault tree whose AND-gate relies on A/B independence (SF-003-TL, SF-005-TL, rudder/aileron supply pairs). Verify minimum separation between bleed duct and HV feeder; pressure-boundary penetration integrity.

zsaData.desc: Engine nacelle 1 (representative of 610–640, nacelles 1–4) — high energy, flammable fluid, DESIGNATED FIRE ZONE per §25.1181. Houses engine, FADEC, generator, EDP, dual fire-detection loops, extinguisher plumbing. HV feeder and bleed ducts originate here.
zsaData.equip: Engine, dual-channel FADEC, 150 kVA generator, engine-driven hydraulic pump (EDP), dual-loop fire detection, extinguisher plumbing
zsaData.interference: Designated fire zone (§25.1181(a)(1)/(2)/(6)). Co-locates the engine (high-energy rotating machinery), flammable fluid (fuel + hydraulic), an electrical source (generator) and the accessory drive. FADEC dual channels take power from four different sources across the four engines so no single bus loss affects more than one engine (§5.1.5) — verify within-nacelle channel separation.
zsaData.mitigation: Fire-zone drainage and ventilation per §25.1187 (complete drainage, ventilation to prevent flammable-vapour accumulation); dual detection loops routed on opposite sides, separately clipped (§5.12.5); confirm FADEC channel/power separation; fireproof lines/fittings. Cross-link Rotor Burst (§25.903(d)(1)/AC 20-128A) and Engine Burst (§25.901(c)) PRAs.

zsaData.desc: Left main gear bay (mirrored by 720 right) — unpressurised, overheat detection fitted. Houses three bogies each, brake lines A and B, steering and brake harnesses. Brake hydraulic lines A/B transit each bay.
zsaData.equip: Three main bogies, brake hydraulic lines A and B (adjacent, separately clipped), steering harness, brake harness, overheat detection
zsaData.interference: Brake hydraulic lines for systems A and B run through each main gear bay in adjacent but separately clipped/shielded bundles, sharing the bay (§5.6.5, recorded zonal item) — a co-location that could couple normal (B) and alternate (A) braking. Tire burst / flailing tread is an in-bay physical threat to both bundles.
zsaData.mitigation: CMA of the A/B brake-line co-location against the dual-brake-supply independence claim; verify separate clipping/shielding adequacy; steering and brake harnesses confirmed on opposite sides of bay (§5.6.5). Cross-link Tire Burst PRA-99249 (§25.734) — flailing tread bearing on co-located brake lines.

zsaData.desc: Nose gear bay — unpressurised. Houses nose unit, steering actuator, tow disconnect.
zsaData.equip: Twin-wheel steerable nose unit, hydraulic steering actuator, mechanical tow disconnect
zsaData.interference: Steering actuator and mechanical tow disconnect co-located; tow-disconnect misconfiguration is a maintenance/ground-handling error candidate (misconfiguration, not failure — model explicitly per NASA-FTH guidance if it feeds a tree). Tire burst in-bay threat.
zsaData.mitigation: Verify tow-disconnect cannot be left disengaged undetected; nose-gear downlock dual proximity sensing integrity; steering harness routing. Cross-link Tire Burst PRA-99249.

zsaData.desc: Aft fuselage and empennage — mixed environment; APU compartment is a DESIGNATED FIRE ZONE per §25.1181(a)(4). Houses rudder control runs, stabiliser heater feeders, APU compartment. Rudder control runs, stabiliser heater feeders, LV signal, data channels transit.
zsaData.equip: Upper/lower rudder control runs (opposite sides), stabiliser heater feeders, APU + APU generator, APU fire detection + dedicated bottle
zsaData.interference: Mixed zone containing the APU fire zone. Upper and lower rudder segment runs on opposite sides of the aft fuselage (§5.3.5) preserve split-rudder independence — verify. Stabiliser heater feeders routed on the opposite side from rudder control runs (§5.10.5). APU compartment flammable-fluid + ignition source.
zsaData.mitigation: APU compartment drainage/ventilation per §25.1187 and fire-zone isolation per §25.1181(a)(4); confirm upper/lower rudder run separation preserves yaw-control redundancy (SF-005 trees); confirm stabiliser-feeder vs rudder-run separation; automatic APU shutdown/fuel-isolation on APU fire (§5.12.4). Cross-link Cabin/hold fire PRA-99256.

cmaData.subject: G-009 roll-command voting independence (page-1788202918632-29 node 27) — SF-003-M2 Uncommanded roll motion
cmaData.claim: Independence principle: Three dissimilar FCCs on different electrical sources vote on command; a single erroneous command is contained by the other two channels.. An erroneous roll command from one FCC is outvoted by the remaining two of three dissimilar flight control computers.
cmaData.findings: Common Failure/Error Source Concern | Effect on the Principle | Mitigating Factor or Lack of Independence. (1) Common air/inertial data: three FCCs consume shared air-data/inertial reference data; a corrupted reference driving all three defeats the vote (SDD 5.3.4). Partial mitigation: three ADIRUs, one on DC essential. (2) Common voting/monitor design: the voting algorithm is common across channels; a common specification error in the vote logic is not outvoted. (3) Software dissimilarity gap: software is developed by only two teams across three computers, so at least two channels share a software baseline and a common software fault could carry the vote. (4) Common environment: FCC 2 sits in zone 300, FCC 1 in zone 120, FCC 3 in zone 400 — installed in three separate bays, so co-location does not defeat this claim.
cmaData.mitigation:
Retain three-way voting; require the shared reference data to be independently validated/cross-compared upstream; require the vote/monitor logic to be dissimilar or independently verified; substantiate the two-team software dissimilarity argument against a common-mode software fault surviving the vote.
Independence requirements (dev / PASA-PSSA):
• The FCS shall detect and reject a corrupted air/inertial reference before it drives the roll command in more than one channel.
• The FCS voting and monitor design shall be substantiated against a common specification or software error surviving the three-way vote.
Verification (SSA/ASA): VERIFICATION-phase note (SSA/ASA): confirm the as-built ADIRU cross-comparison and the software dissimilarity allocation across the three FCCs close the shared-data and common-software contributors; feed any residual common-cause contributor into the SF-003-M2 tree.

cmaData.subject: G-011 aileron dual-hydraulic independence (page-1788202918642-308 node 34) — SF-003-TL Complete loss of roll control
cmaData.claim: Independence principle: Each aileron is driven by two actuators supplied from different hydraulic systems (B and C); a single hydraulic loss leaves the aileron powered.. Loss of aileron control requires coincident loss of hydraulic system B AND hydraulic system C.
cmaData.findings: Common Failure/Error Source Concern | Effect on the Principle | Mitigating Factor or Lack of Independence. (1) Shared routing: HYD A and B share a wing-root run, but THIS gate pairs B and C; HYD C is routed separately along the opposite side, so the recorded A/B wing-root commonality does not defeat B-and-C (SDD 5.4.5, §4). (2) Common environment — zone 300: HYD A/B wing-root run and HYD C both transit the mid hold/mid equipment bay (zone 300); a zonal event there could strike both B and C runs. (3) Common design: systems B and C are separate in fluid and pumping (B engine-driven, C electric-motor/RAT), reducing common-mode pump/source failure. (4) Particular risk: a zone-300 event (recorded convergence zone) is the credible common cause and must be reconciled with ZSA zone 300.
cmaData.mitigation:
Maintain B and C on separated routes through zone 300 with defined minimum separation and shielding; require the zonal analysis of zone 300 to confirm no single event takes both B and C runs; carry the residual as a common-cause contributor if separation cannot be assured.
Independence requirements (dev / PASA-PSSA):
• Hydraulic systems B and C shall be installed with sufficient physical separation through zone 300 that no single zonal event disables both aileron supplies.
Verification (SSA/ASA): VERIFICATION-phase note (SSA/ASA): confirm as-built B/C separation in zone 300 against the zonal (ZSA) finding for that zone; where separation is not achieved, add an explicit common-cause contributor to the SF-003-TL tree beneath node 34.

cmaData.subject: G-012 all-roll-surface actuation independence (page-1788202918642-308 node 33) — SF-003-TL Complete loss of roll control
cmaData.claim: Independence principle: Roll is by two-segment ailerons AND multi-function spoilers; loss of all roll actuation needs both surface groups lost together.. Loss of all roll surface actuation requires coincident loss of aileron control AND loss of multi-function spoiler roll augmentation.
cmaData.findings: Common Failure/Error Source Concern | Effect on the Principle | Mitigating Factor or Lack of Independence. (1) Common hydraulic resource: ailerons are on HYD B/C and the multi-function spoilers also draw hydraulic motive power; a hydraulic system common to both surface groups would defeat the AND. The SDD does not state which systems supply the spoilers, so the shared-resource exposure between aileron and spoiler supply cannot be confirmed. (2) Common environment — zone 300: the hydraulic runs supplying both groups transit zone 300, the recorded convergence zone. (3) Common command origin: both surface groups are commanded by the same three FCCs; a common FCC-level roll-command fault reaches ailerons and spoilers together. (4) Common design: hydraulic systems are separate in fluid and pumping, limiting cross-system fluid coupling.
cmaData.mitigation:
Require the multi-function spoiler hydraulic supply to be identified and separated from the aileron supply so no single hydraulic system feeds both groups; maintain zone-300 separation; treat a common FCC roll-command fault as a shared cause between the two surface groups.
Independence requirements (dev / PASA-PSSA):
• The multi-function spoiler roll supply shall not share a single hydraulic system whose loss also disables aileron actuation.
• A common flight-control-computer roll-command fault reaching both ailerons and spoilers shall be modelled as a shared cause under node 33.
Verification (SSA/ASA): VERIFICATION-phase note (SSA/ASA): once the spoiler hydraulic allocation is released to engineering, confirm no single hydraulic system or FCC command path defeats both surface groups; add the confirmed shared cause as a common-cause contributor under node 33 of the SF-003-TL tree.

cmaData.subject: G-013 — Loss of all three flight control computers (SF-003-TL top-gate independence)
cmaData.claim: Independence principle: Independence of the three flight control computers underpinning the SF-003-TL AND gate (loss of all three FCC).. The three dissimilar flight control computers (FCC 1/2/3) fail independently, each in a separate bay on a separate electrical source, so their coincident loss is an AND.
cmaData.findings: Common Failure/Error Source Concern | Effect on the Principle | Mitigating Factor or Lack of Independence. (1) Common electrical resource — generator part-number commonality: all four 150 kVA generators are a single part number; a generic generator design/lot fault degrades multiple main buses feeding the FCCs. Mitigating: FCCs on three different sources, dissimilar bus power control units, staggered overhaul. (2) Installation co-location — zone 300: FCC 2 is installed in the mid equipment bay (zone 300), the convergence zone through which HV/LV feeders, HYD A/B, HYD C, fuel gallery, bleed cross-bleed manifold and both data channels transit; a zonal event there strikes FCC 2 and co-located routing. Mitigating: FCC 1 (zone 120) and FCC 3 (zone 400) are in separate bays. (3) Common design/software — dissimilarity argument: software developed by one of two teams under a dissimilarity argument; a specification-level common error can defeat dissimilarity across all three. Mitigating: three dissimilar computers, two-team split. (4) Common data — corrupted air/inertial data driving all three FCCs (SF-003-M anchor gate node 22 shows this coupling exists at command level). Reconcile with PRA-99253 HIRF and lightning §25.1316 as potential all-channel environmental cause.
cmaData.mitigation:
Confirm no single bus loss affects more than one FCC (SDD asserts this for FADEC — verify it holds for FCC feeds); treat generator part-number commonality as a common-cause contributor to the SF-003-TL tree rather than leaving a clean 3-way AND; zonal analysis of zone 300 against FCC 2 loss with co-located routing; substantiate the software dissimilarity argument feeds the DAL reduction that rests on this AND (App P).
Independence requirements (dev / PASA-PSSA):
• The three flight control computer electrical feeds shall be arranged such that no single generator, bus, or bus-tie failure removes more than one flight control computer.
• A common-cause contributor representing generator part-number commonality shall be modelled explicitly in the SF-003-TL fault tree rather than relying on independent-failure logic alone.
• The zonal analysis shall demonstrate that no single event in zone 300 defeats the independence of FCC 2 from FCC 1 and FCC 3.

aiRequirements: The consolidated crew-alerting channels annunciating uncommanded pitch motion shall not share electrical supply or processing with the flight control computer capable of issuing a spurious pitch command.

cmaData.subject: SF-004-TL — Complete loss of pitch control: powered-actuation ∩ mechanical-reversion independence, incl. elevator HYD A∩HYD C actuation AND
cmaData.claim: Independence principle: Physical and functional independence of the two elevator hydraulic supplies (A, C) and independence of the mechanical reversion path from all powered/FCC command paths.. Loss of powered elevator/stabiliser actuation is independent of loss of the mechanical reversion path; within the powered branch, elevator actuation from HYD A and HYD C fails independently.
cmaData.findings: HYD A and HYD C are separate circuits (separate fluid, pumping, distribution); HYD C routed separately from A/B (zone 400→300→200) while A/B share the wing-root run (zone 530/300/540) — so the A/B shared run does not directly couple the A∩C pair. Residual co-location: HYD C, HYD A/B run, and FCC 2 all converge in zone 300 (mid hold / mid equipment bay). Mechanical reversion to stabiliser trim and lower rudder is a dissimilar path independent of the three FCCs.
cmaData.mitigation: Maintain HYD A and HYD C on separate routes through zone 300; assess zone-300 convergence under ZSA as a co-location common-cause candidate. Apply dissimilar/independent rigging and maintenance controls to the mechanical reversion linkage to avoid a common rigging error defeating the reversion-vs-powered independence.
cmaData.aiPrinciple: Physical and functional independence of the two elevator hydraulic supplies (A, C) and independence of the mechanical reversion path from all powered/FCC command paths.

cmaData.subject: SF-005-M3 — Undetected yaw response error: dual crew-alerting channel independence (annunciation AND)
cmaData.claim: Independence principle: Independence of the two crew-alerting processing channels that annunciate an erroneous yaw response.. An erroneous yaw response and simultaneous failure of both consolidated crew-alerting channels are independent events (alerting channels 1 and 2 fail independently).
cmaData.findings: SDD states alerting is 'driven by two independent processing channels'; the SDD does not state they are dissimilar in software or supplied from separated electrical sources. Both channels are AVI processing and consume the alerting data path — a common alerting-application software fault, or a common electrical source, is a candidate common cause defeating the channel-1 ∩ channel-2 AND. The erroneous-yaw-response branch (FCC/rudder ACE/air-data) is a separate functional path.
cmaData.mitigation: Require the two alerting channels to be dissimilar in processing/software and supplied from separated electrical sources (e.g. one on DC essential); verify no shared connector/routing. Where the AND-gate independence underpins the undetected (crew-unaware) classification, a failed independence invalidates the latency assumption.
cmaData.aiPrinciple: Independence of the two crew-alerting processing channels that annunciate an erroneous yaw response.

cmaData.subject: SF-005-M4 — Undetected uncommanded yaw motion: dual crew-alerting channel independence (annunciation AND) and shared reference feeds
cmaData.claim: Independence principle: Independence of the two crew-alerting channels annunciating uncommanded yaw motion, and independence of the motion-generating paths (rudder segment actuation, ACE runaway, FCC spurious command).. An uncommanded yaw motion and simultaneous failure of both consolidated crew-alerting channels are independent; the uncommanded-motion contributors do not share a common cause with the annunciation channels.
cmaData.findings: Same dual-alerting-channel concern as SF-005-M3: SDD asserts two independent channels but does not evidence dissimilar software or separated supplies, so a common alerting design/software fault or common electrical source is a candidate common cause. Motion branch: FCC spurious rudder command and ACE runaway share air-data/inertial reference feeds as a potential common input; upper/lower rudder segments have their own actuation and own hydraulic supply (A vs B), so the two-segment motion sources are physically separated.
cmaData.mitigation: As SF-005-M3: mandate dissimilar alerting channels on separated supplies. Additionally verify FCC voting/monitoring is independent of the shared air-data/inertial reference feeding the spurious-command path so a corrupted reference does not both cause and mask the motion.
cmaData.aiPrinciple: Independence of the two crew-alerting channels annunciating uncommanded yaw motion, and independence of the motion-generating paths (rudder segment actuation, ACE runaway, FCC spurious command).

cmaData.subject: SF-005-TL — Complete loss of yaw control: independence of upper rudder segment (HYD A) vs lower rudder segment (HYD B) vs mechanical reversion
cmaData.claim: Independence principle: Two-segment split rudder on independent hydraulic supplies A and B, with mechanical reversion to the lower segment.. Upper and lower rudder segments fail independently because each has its own actuation and its own hydraulic supply (A upper, B lower), with mechanical reversion to the lower segment as a third path.
cmaData.findings: HYD A and HYD B share a wing-root run where both cross the pressure boundary (zones 530/540/300) per SDD §5.4.5/§5.3.5 — a single event in that shared run is a common cause to the upper (A) and lower (B) supply, defeating the AND-gate independence between the two segment-loss branches. Rudder control runs to upper and lower segments are on opposite sides of the aft fuselage (zone 800), which supports independence of the mechanical-reversion path. EPS is a shared resource to actuator control electronics on both segments (common resource). Development-phase CMA (supports PSSA). Category exposure: Common Resources (HYD A/B shared wing-root run; EPS); Installation Design (co-location in zones 530/540/300).
cmaData.mitigation:
Confirm and substantiate physical/spatial separation, or a barrier, on the HYD A and HYD B lines within the shared wing-root run so no single event takes both; verify rudder segment control-run separation in zone 800; retain the shared wing-root run as a dedicated zonal (ZSA) item and reconcile with PRA (rotor burst / fire in aft fuselage).
Independence requirements (dev / PASA-PSSA):
• The HYD A and HYD B rudder supply lines shall be separated within the shared wing-root run such that no single physical event disables both rudder segments.
Verification (SSA/ASA): SSA/ASA to confirm as-installed separation of HYD A and HYD B in zones 530/540/300 and the zone-800 rudder control-run separation, closing the independence requirement.
cmaData.aiPrinciple: Two-segment split rudder on independent hydraulic supplies A and B, with mechanical reversion to the lower segment.
aiRequirements: The HYD A and HYD B rudder supply lines shall be separated within the shared wing-root run such that no single physical event disables both rudder segments.
cmaData.aiVerification: SSA/ASA to confirm as-installed separation of HYD A and HYD B in zones 530/540/300 and the zone-800 rudder control-run separation, closing the independence requirement.

cmaData.subject: SF-006-PL3 — Undetected partial loss of high-lift augmentation (asymmetric): independence of asymmetric-mismatch source vs asymmetry-monitor annunciation
cmaData.claim: Independence principle: Two independent power drive units through a common torque shaft with asymmetry brakes at each section, monitored by an asymmetry annunciation.. An asymmetric high-lift mismatch and the failure of the asymmetry monitor to annunciate it are independent events combined under the AND gate.
cmaData.findings: The two high-lift PDUs drive through a COMMON torque shaft with asymmetry brakes at each section per SDD §5.3.2 — the common torque shaft is a shared mechanical element whose disconnect/torque-shaft failure is the very mismatch source, and its independence from the asymmetry monitor sensing must be demonstrated. Common-design concern: the asymmetry monitor sensing/annunciation path and the mismatch-detection logic. EPS is a shared resource to the drive control and the monitor (common resource). Development-phase CMA (supports PSSA). Category exposure: Common Resources (common torque shaft; EPS); Development/Design (common asymmetry-monitor design).
cmaData.mitigation:
Substantiate that the asymmetry monitor senses section position independently of the drive train it is monitoring (independent position pick-off, independent supply); confirm the asymmetry brakes and the annunciation are not defeated by the same torque-shaft/drive fault.
Independence requirements (dev / PASA-PSSA):
• The asymmetry monitoring and annunciation shall sense high-lift section position independently of the power drive train, so that a drive or torque-shaft fault cannot simultaneously cause and mask an asymmetry.
Verification (SSA/ASA): SSA/ASA to confirm the asymmetry monitor position sensing and supply are independent of the high-lift drive train, closing the independence requirement.

aiRequirements: The asymmetry monitoring and annunciation shall sense high-lift section position independently of the power drive train, so that a drive or torque-shaft fault cannot simultaneously cause and mask an asymmetry.
cmaData.aiVerification: SSA/ASA to confirm the asymmetry monitor position sensing and supply are independent of the high-lift drive train, closing the independence requirement.

cmaData.subject: SF-007-TL — Complete loss of ground support and landing-load absorption: independence of left main-gear support vs right main-gear support
cmaData.claim: Independence principle: Six three-wheel main bogies, three per side, with retraction/extension on HYD A and a free-fall alternate extension independent of hydraulic pressure.. Loss of left main-gear support and loss of right main-gear support are independent, combined under an AND gate.
cmaData.findings: Both left and right main-gear support branches depend on HYD A for normal extension (SDD §5.6.2) — a single loss of HYD A is common to both sides, defeating the AND-gate independence unless the free-fall alternate extension is credited; the fault trees already list 'Loss of HYD A extension with free-fall alternate' as an input on both sides (nodes 109/113), so the shared HYD A is the common resource and the free-fall path is the mitigating independent means. Common resource: HYD A. Development-phase CMA (supports PSSA). Category exposure: Common Resources (HYD A extension supply shared left/right).
cmaData.mitigation:
Credit and substantiate the free-fall alternate extension as independent of HYD A so that loss of HYD A does not by itself deny down-and-locked on both sides; confirm the two independent downlock proximity circuits per unit are not common-cause.
Independence requirements (dev / PASA-PSSA):
• The free-fall alternate gear extension shall be independent of hydraulic system A such that loss of HYD A alone cannot deny main-gear down-and-locked on both sides.
Verification (SSA/ASA): SSA/ASA to confirm the free-fall alternate extension and the dual downlock sensing are independent of HYD A, closing the independence requirement.

aiRequirements: The free-fall alternate gear extension shall be independent of hydraulic system A such that loss of HYD A alone cannot deny main-gear down-and-locked on both sides.
cmaData.aiVerification: SSA/ASA to confirm the free-fall alternate extension and the dual downlock sensing are independent of HYD A, closing the independence requirement.

cmaData.subject: SF-010-M2 — Nose door lock indication: proximity sensing path vs. mechanical-linkage visual indicator independence
cmaData.claim: Independence principle: Dual dissimilar, independently-routed lock sensing — proximity harness (pin position) and mechanical linkage driving a visual indicator — with no shared element.. Erroneous lock indication AND coincident loss of the independent cross-check indication are both required (AND gate id 114); the two sensing paths are dissimilar and independently routed.
cmaData.findings: Installation-design / environment coupling: both sensing paths terminate at the flight-deck (zone 130) and cross the zone boundary at the flight-deck bulkhead; the proximity sensing harness transits 110→120→130. A single event at the bulkhead-penetration region or common flight-deck installation could affect both. Development/design coupling: shared calibration/rigging of the sensing harness and the mechanical indicator at a single maintenance action is a candidate common-cause. Operation coupling: SF-010-M relies on crew cross-check of the visual indicator; a crew failure to consult it removes the second path.
cmaData.mitigation:
SDD claims the harness is routed opposite the door actuation power and separated from the indicator linkage throughout, with two SEPARATED bulkhead penetrations (§5.7.5). Confirm minimum separation is maintained at the flight-deck bulkhead region and that no single physical event takes both penetrations; verify the dissimilarity (electrical proximity vs. mechanical linkage) precludes a common design/calibration error; confirm the take-off configuration monitor consumes both channels independently.
Independence requirements (dev / PASA-PSSA):
• The proximity sensing harness and the mechanical indicator linkage shall be installed such that no single physical event at the flight-deck bulkhead defeats both sensing paths.
• The lock indication and cross-check shall be verified as free of common calibration/rigging action under a single maintenance task.
Verification (SSA/ASA): SSA/ASA: confirm by installation drawing and zonal (ZSA zone 130 / zone 110) review that the two bulkhead penetrations remain physically separated; confirm dissimilarity precludes common design error; record whether the crew visual cross-check is a credited independent path.

cmaData.subject: SF-010-TL — Nose door latch retention vs. lock-pin retention independence
cmaData.claim: Independence principle: Twelve rotary latches on a common torque shaft plus eight independent locking pins on a separate actuator and separate hydraulic supply, so latches cannot back-drive while pins are engaged.. Loss of latch retention (twelve rotary latches, gate 122) AND loss of lock-pin retention (eight pins, gate 125) are both required (AND gate id 121); latches and pins are on separate drives and separate hydraulic supplies.
cmaData.findings: Common-resource coupling within the latch set: the twelve latches are driven by a COMMON torque shaft — already an explicit basic event (gate 123) — so latch retention has no internal redundancy against a torque-shaft failure. Installation-design / environment coupling: latches and pins are co-located in zone 110 (nose visor structure), exposing both mechanisms to a common mechanical/impact and thermal environment on a single structural element; the visor is a single load path treated as structure. Maintenance coupling: a single maintenance/rigging action on the visor could affect both latch and pin mechanisms. Particular risk: bird strike / hail on the forward-facing nose visor (zone 110) is a candidate to strike both mechanisms.
cmaData.mitigation:
SDD provides genuine resource split: pins are driven by a separate actuator on a SEPARATE hydraulic supply from the visor/latch drive (HYD A), and the pins prevent latch back-drive — this supports the AND. Confirm the latch common torque shaft is captured in the tree (it is, gate 123); confirm zonal (ZSA zone 110) and particular-risk (bird strike / hail on forward-facing structure) analyses show the two mechanisms are not defeated by one impact; confirm separate maintenance tasks / independent rig checks for latches and pins.
Independence requirements (dev / PASA-PSSA):
• The lock-pin hydraulic supply and actuator shall be independent of the visor/latch drive supply such that no single supply loss defeats both latch and pin retention.
• The nose visor zonal and particular-risk analyses shall demonstrate that a single impact (bird strike / hail) or common maintenance action does not simultaneously defeat latch and lock-pin retention.
Verification (SSA/ASA): SSA/ASA: confirm the common torque-shaft dependency is modelled (gate 123 basic event); confirm from ZSA (zone 110) and PRA (bird strike / hail) that co-location does not defeat both mechanisms; confirm separate maintenance procedures for latch and pin systems.

cmaData.subject: SF-011-PL3 — Longitudinal restraint loss vs. tension-loss annunciation independence
cmaData.claim: Independence principle: Strap/saddle restraint with a continuous instrumented tension monitoring loop annunciating loss of tension, so a restraint failure is detected and crew-aware.. Loss of longitudinal restraint (gate 129) AND failure to annunciate loss of tension (gate 132) are both required (AND gate id 128); restraint load path and detection path are independent.
cmaData.findings: Common-resource coupling in the detection path: the tension monitoring is a SINGLE instrumented loop running the full hold length (zones 200→300→400) — it is the only detection path for every station, so a single loop break defeats annunciation for the whole hold; gate 132 already carries this as basic events (ids 133/134). Installation-design coupling: the single loop shares the hold zone with the fuel-gallery vent and the left-side electrical route (§5.8.5, a recorded item), a co-location that could damage the loop. Common-resource coupling across paths: both the winches (restraint) and the tension loop (detection) consume EPS electrical power (§5.8.4), so a loss of the left-side electrical route in the hold is a candidate common cause of both restraint winch power and loop indication.
cmaData.mitigation:
SDD records the single-loop coverage as an item to examine (§5.8.3) and the shared hold zone as a recorded item (§5.8.5). Confirm the tension loop electrical supply is independent of the winch power feed so an electrical event does not take both; confirm zonal (ZSA zone 200/300/400) review of the shared left-side route; note that with no in-flight restraint adjustment, detection independence is the sole credited mitigation for crew awareness.
Independence requirements (dev / PASA-PSSA):
• The restraint tension monitoring loop electrical supply shall be independent of the restraint winch power feed such that a single electrical event does not defeat both restraint and its annunciation.
• The single instrumented tension loop routing and its co-location with the fuel-gallery vent and left-side electrical route shall be substantiated by zonal analysis for the full hold length.
Verification (SSA/ASA): SSA/ASA: confirm loop supply independence from winch power; confirm by ZSA (zones 200/300/400) that the shared left-side hold route does not defeat both restraint and detection; record the single-loop coverage as an accepted architectural limitation or drive a requirement for loop segmentation.

The single instrumented tension loop routing and its co-location with the fuel-gallery vent and left-side electrical route shall be substantiated by zonal analysis for the full hold length.

cmaData.subject: SF-011-TL — Complete loss of longitudinal payload restraint (AND-gate independence: all strap/saddle load paths lost AND hold floor hard-point attachment lost)
cmaData.claim: Independence principle: Redundancy of the nine saddle / two-strap restraint set, with the hard-point load path as an independent second leg.. The two AND-gate legs — restraint strap/saddle load paths and the hold floor hard-point attachment — fail independently.
cmaData.findings: Common Resource — electrical: all nine winches and the tension monitoring loop draw on a single EPS feed; loss of that feed defeats tensioning across every station simultaneously (leg 'all strap/saddle load paths fail'). Installation Design / Environment: the restraint tension monitoring loop is a single instrumented left-side run transiting zones 200/300/400 sharing the hold zone with the left-side electrical route and fuel gallery vent — a zonal event (fire/fuel) can strike detection and load-path monitoring together. Development/Design: no redundancy exists in the hold floor hard points, so the 'hard-point attachment loss' leg has no internal diversity. This is a Part 25 special-condition area (single unitised payload) for which existing restraint requirements were not written.
cmaData.mitigation:
Substantiate the hard-point load path by structural analysis and Particular Risk Analysis (structure, not functional redundancy). Add a common-cause contributor for the shared winch electrical feed to the restraint fault tree. Segregate or duplicate the tension monitoring loop off the single left-side route, or justify the single loop against a zonal hazard.
Independence requirements (dev / PASA-PSSA):
• The cargo restraint winch tensioning function shall not depend on a single electrical feed such that one feed loss defeats tensioning at every station.
• The hold floor hard-point attachment load path shall be substantiated by structural analysis and Particular Risk Analysis independent of the strap/saddle functional load path.
cmaData.aiPrinciple: Redundancy of the nine saddle / two-strap restraint set, with the hard-point load path as an independent second leg.
aiRequirements: The cargo restraint winch tensioning function shall not depend on a single electrical feed such that one feed loss defeats tensioning at every station.
The hold floor hard-point attachment load path shall be substantiated by structural analysis and Particular Risk Analysis independent of the strap/saddle functional load path.

cmaData.subject: SF-016-M3 — Undetected erroneous flight and navigation information (AND-gate independence: erroneous data presented AND not detected/annunciated)
cmaData.claim: Independence principle: Independence of the standby instrument from the primary displays — no shared supply, sensor or processing — supporting the cross-check that detects erroneous primary data.. Erroneous flight/navigation data generation and the detection/annunciation leg (reference-unit cross-comparison AND independent standby agreement) fail independently.
cmaData.findings: Common Resource — electrical: the independent standby instrument is supplied from the DC essential bus, and one of the three air-data inertial reference units is ALSO supplied from the DC essential bus; a DC-essential loss is a shared contributor that can degrade both the standby-agreement check and one reference source at once. Development/Design: the three reference units are of a common type — a common design/software error would corrupt primary and could survive cross-comparison. Mitigating: the three display processors and FCC are in three separate bays (zones 120/300/400) and the two network channels share no connector or penetration, which supports the physical-independence part of the claim; the standby instrument is stated to share no supply, no sensor and no processing with the primary displays — this conflicts with the DC-essential observation for ADIRU 3 and must be reconciled.
cmaData.mitigation:
Confirm the standby-instrument supply is genuinely independent of any reference unit feeding the primary comparison; if ADIRU 3 and the standby share the DC essential bus, add a common-cause contributor for DC-essential loss to the detection leg. Substantiate dissimilarity/monitoring against a common reference-unit design error.
Independence requirements (dev / PASA-PSSA):
• The integrated standby instrument shall share no electrical source with any air-data inertial reference unit relied upon for the primary-display erroneous-data cross-comparison.
• A common design or software error in the air-data inertial reference units shall not defeat both the primary presentation and its cross-comparison detection.

aiRequirements: The integrated standby instrument shall share no electrical source with any air-data inertial reference unit relied upon for the primary-display erroneous-data cross-comparison.

cmaData.subject: SF-018-TL2 — Undetected complete loss of fire and overheat detection (AND-gate independence: complete loss of detection AND loss of crew warning/annunciation)
cmaData.claim: Independence principle: Independence of the detection function from the crew-alerting annunciation function, so that a detection loss is still annunciated and an annunciation loss still leaves detection.. Complete loss of fire/overheat detection and loss of the crew warning/annunciation path fail independently.
cmaData.findings: Common Resource — electrical: the tree already shows 'Loss of DC essential bus supply to fire detection' (node 156) on the detection leg AND 'Loss of DC essential bus supply to crew alerting' (node 159) on the annunciation leg — an IDENTICAL shared resource on BOTH legs of the AND. A single DC-essential loss therefore drives both legs simultaneously and the AND independence is not genuine for that contributor; it belongs as a repeated event / dedicated common-cause gate rather than two separate basic events. Mitigating: fire discharge circuits are supplied from the hot battery bus so they remain available with all generation lost, and the two detection loops per zone are routed on opposite sides — but that mitigation protects discharge and per-zone detection, not the shared DC-essential supply to detection processing and alerting.
cmaData.mitigation:
Model the DC essential bus loss as a single repeated event across nodes 156 and 159 (or a common-cause gate above the AND) so the tree does not credit false independence. Substantiate that fire/overheat detection and crew alerting do not both rest solely on the DC essential bus, or provide an independent supply to one leg (e.g. hot battery bus, as used for discharge).
Independence requirements (dev / PASA-PSSA):
• Fire/overheat detection and its crew annunciation shall not both depend solely on the DC essential bus such that a single bus loss defeats both detection and warning.
• The DC essential bus loss shall be represented as a single repeated event across the detection and alerting legs of the SF-018-TL2 fault tree.
cmaData.aiPrinciple: Independence of the detection function from the crew-alerting annunciation function, so that a detection loss is still annunciated and an annunciation loss still leaves detection.
aiRequirements: Fire/overheat detection and its crew annunciation shall not both depend solely on the DC essential bus such that a single bus loss defeats both detection and warning.
The DC essential bus loss shall be represented as a single repeated event across the detection and alerting legs of the SF-018-TL2 fault tree.
